title.zh: 卷九十八 列傳第五十八 氐胡
title.raw: 卷九十八 列傳第五十八 氐胡 Volume 98 Biographies 58: Di Hu

sentences.zh: 略陽清水氐楊氏，秦、漢以來，世居隴右，為豪族。

translations.literal: The Di clan Yang of Qingshui in Lueyang, since the Qin and Han dynasties, had for generations dwelt in Longyou and were a powerful clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang clan of the Di people at Qingshui in Lueyang had lived in Longyou as a powerful family since Qin and Han times.

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝建安中，有楊騰者，為部落大帥。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an era under Emperor Xian of Han, there was one Yang Teng, who served as great chieftain of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jian'an reign of Emperor Xian of Han, a man named Yang Teng rose to be great chieftain of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 騰子駒，勇健多計略，始徙仇池。

translations.literal: Teng's son Ju was brave, strong, and full of stratagems; he was the first to move the clan to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Teng's son Ju was bold, resourceful, and the first to relocate the clan to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 仇池地方百頃，因以百頃為號，四面斗絕，高平地方二十餘里，羊腸蟠道，三十六回。

translations.literal: The territory of Chouchi was one hundred qing in area; they therefore took "Hundred Qing" as their designation. On all four sides it rose sheer; the level ground above covered more than twenty li, with a coiling goat-path track of thirty-six switchbacks.
translations.idiomatic: Chouchi covered about a hundred qing of ground, and they took "Hundred Qing" as their name. Cliffs ringed it on every side; the plateau on top stretched more than twenty li, reached only by a winding goat track with thirty-six bends.

sentences.zh: 山上豐水泉，煮土成鹽。

translations.literal: On the mountain were abundant springs; by boiling the soil they obtained salt.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain had plentiful springs, and they made salt by boiling the local soil.

sentences.zh: 駒後有名千萬者，魏拜為百頃氐王。

translations.literal: After Ju there was one named Qianwan; Wei enfeoffed him as King of the Di of Hundred Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was succeeded by Qianwan, whom Wei recognized as King of the Hundred-Qing Di.

sentences.zh: 千萬子孫名飛龍，漸強盛，晉武假征西將軍，[1]還居略陽。

translations.literal: Qianwan's grandson was named Feilong; he gradually grew powerful, and Emperor Wu of Jin provisionally appointed him General Who Pacifies the West[1] and he returned to dwell in Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwan's grandson Feilong grew steadily stronger; Emperor Wu of Jin gave him the provisional title General Who Pacifies the West[1], and he moved back to Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 無子，養外甥令狐氏子為子，名戊搜。

translations.literal: Having no son, he adopted as his son his sister's son of the Linghu clan and named him Wusou.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted his sister's son from the Linghu clan and named him Wusou.

sentences.zh: [2]晉惠帝元康六年，避齊萬年之亂，率部落四千家，還保百頃，自號輔國將軍、右賢王。

translations.literal: [2]In the sixth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, to escape the turmoil of Qi Wannian, he led four thousand families of the tribe back to hold Hundred Qing and styled himself General Who Assists the State and Right Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: [2]In the sixth year of Yuankang (296), fleeing the revolt of Qi Wannian, Wusou led four thousand tribal households back to defend Hundred Qing and took the titles General Who Assists the State and Right Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 關中人士奔流者多依之，戊搜延納撫接，欲去者則衞護資遣之。

translations.literal: Many of the gentry of Guanzhong who fled in disorder relied on him; Wusou received and comforted them, and those who wished to leave he escorted and supplied for their journey.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from Guanzhong flocked to him; Wusou welcomed and cared for them, and those who wished to leave he escorted and sent off with supplies.

sentences.zh: 愍帝以為驃騎將軍、左賢王。

translations.literal: Emperor Min appointed him Cavalry General-in-Chief and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min made him Cavalry General-in-Chief and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 時南陽王保在上邽，又以戊搜子難敵為征南將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Nanyang Bao was at Shanggui, and he also appointed Wusou's son Nandi as General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bao of Nanyang was then at Shanggui and also named Wusou's son Nandi General Who Campaigns South.

sentences.zh: 建興五年，戊搜卒，難敵襲位。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianxing, Wusou died and Nandi succeeded to his position.
translations.idiomatic: Wusou died in the fifth year of Jianxing (317), and Nandi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 與堅頭分部曲，[3]難敵號左賢王，屯下辯，堅頭號右賢王，屯河池。

translations.literal: He and Jiantou divided the tribal forces;[3] Nandi styled himself Left Worthy King and encamped at Xiabian, while Jiantou styled himself Right Worthy King and encamped at Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jiantou split the tribal forces;[3] Nandi took the title Left Worthy King and camped at Xiabian, Jiantou the Right Worthy King at Hechi.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興四年，劉曜伐難敵，與堅頭俱奔晉壽，臣於李雄，曜退，復還仇池。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan, Liu Yao attacked Nandi; he and Jiantou both fled to Jinshou and submitted to Li Xiong; when Yao withdrew, they returned again to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taixing (321), Liu Yao attacked Nandi; he and Jiantou fled to Jinshou and submitted to Li Xiong. After Yao withdrew, they returned to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸和九年，難敵卒，子毅立，自號使持節、龍驤將軍、左賢王、下辯公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng, Nandi died; his son Yi succeeded and styled himself Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Dragon-Prancing General, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Xiabian.
translations.idiomatic: Nandi died in the ninth year of Xianhe (334); his son Yi took power as Bearer of the Staff, Dragon-Prancing General, Left Worthy King, and Duke of Xiabian.

sentences.zh: 以堅頭子槃為使持節、冠軍將軍、右賢王、河池公。

translations.literal: He appointed Jiantou's son Pan Bearer of the Staff, Champion General, Right Worthy King, and Duke of Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: He named Jiantou's son Pan Bearer of the Staff, Champion General, Right Worthy King, and Duke of Hechi.

sentences.zh: 咸康元年，遣使稱蕃於晉，以毅為征南，槃征東將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiankang he sent envoys to declare himself a vassal of Jin; Yi was made General Who Campaigns South and Pan General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiankang (335) he sent envoys to submit to Jin; Yi became General Who Campaigns South and Pan General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 三年，毅族兄初襲殺毅，并有其眾，自立為仇池公，臣於石虎。

translations.literal: In the third year, Yi's clansman elder brother Chu murdered Yi by surprise, seized his followers, installed himself as Duke of Chouchi, and submitted to Shi Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Yi's elder clansman Chu ambushed and killed him, absorbed his forces, declared himself Duke of Chouchi, and submitted to Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 後遣使稱蕃於穆帝。

translations.literal: Later he sent envoys to declare himself a vassal of Emperor Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He later sent envoys to submit to Emperor Mu as well.

sentences.zh: 永和三年，以初為使持節、征南將軍、雍州刺史、平羌校尉、仇池公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghe, Chu was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns South, Inspector of Yong Province, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yonghe (347), Chu received Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns South, Inspector of Yong, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 初子國為鎮東將軍、武都太守。

translations.literal: Chu's son Guo was made General Who Guards the East and Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's son Guo became General Who Guards the East and Administrator of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 十年，改封初天水公。

translations.literal: In the tenth year his enfeoffment was changed and Chu was made Duke of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Chu was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 十一年，毅小弟宋奴使姑子梁式王因侍直手刃殺初，初子國率左右誅式王及宋奴，[4]復自立。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Yi's younger brother Songnu had his sister's son Liang Shiwang, while on attendance duty, slay Chu with his own hand; Chu's son Guo led his attendants to execute Shiwang and Songnu[4] and again installed himself in power.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Yi's younger brother Songnu had his nephew Liang Shiwang kill Chu while on palace duty; Guo rallied his men, executed Shiwang and Songnu,[4] and took power again.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍桓溫表國為鎮北將軍、秦州刺史、平羌校尉，國子安為振威將軍、武都太守。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Huan Wen memorialized that Guo be made General Who Guards the North, Inspector of Qin Province, and Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Guo's son An be made General Who Shakes Might and Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, General Who Pacifies the West, recommended Guo as General Who Guards the North, Inspector of Qin, and Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, with Guo's son An as General Who Shakes Might and Administrator of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，國從父楊俊復殺國自立，安奔苻生，俊遣使歸順。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Guo's father's younger cousin Yang Jun again killed Guo and installed himself; An fled to Fu Sheng, and Jun sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Guo's cousin Yang Jun killed him and seized power; An fled to Fu Sheng while Jun sent envoys to declare submission.

sentences.zh: 升平三年，以俊為平西將軍、平羌校尉、仇池公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengping, Jun was made General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shengping (359), Jun was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 四年，俊卒，子世立，復以為冠軍將軍、平羌校尉、武都太守、仇池公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jun died; his son Shi succeeded, and he was again made Champion General, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Administrator of Wudu, and Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun died the next year; his son Shi succeeded and was again named Champion General, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Administrator of Wudu, and Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 海西公太和三年，遷征西將軍、秦州刺史，以世弟統為寧東將軍、武都太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe under Duke Haixi, Shi was transferred to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qin Province; Shi's younger brother Tong was made General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe (368), Shi was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qin; his younger brother Tong became General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 五年，世卒，統廢世子纂自立。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Shi died; Tong deposed Shi's heir Zuan and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shi died in the fifth year (370); Tong deposed the heir Zuan and took the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 纂一名德，聚黨殺統，遣使詣簡文帝自陳，復以纂為平羌校尉、秦州刺史、仇池公。

translations.literal: Zuan, also named De, gathered partisans and killed Tong; he sent envoys to Emperor Jianwen to explain himself, and Zuan was again made Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan—also called De—rallied followers, killed Tong, sent envoys to explain himself to Emperor Jianwen, and was restored as Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Qin, and Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 咸安元年，苻堅遣楊安、苻雅等討纂克之，徙其民於關中，空百頃之地。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xian'an, Fu Jian sent Yang An, Fu Ya, and others to attack Zuan and overcome him; he relocated the people to Guanzhong and emptied the land of Hundred Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xian'an (371), Fu Jian sent Yang An and Fu Ya against Zuan, defeated him, moved the population into Guanzhong, and left Hundred Qing deserted.

sentences.zh: 纂後為楊安所殺。

translations.literal: Later Zuan was killed by Yang An.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was later killed by Yang An.

sentences.zh: 宋奴之死也，二子佛奴、佛狗奔逃關中，苻堅以佛奴為右將軍，佛狗為撫夷護軍。

translations.literal: When Songnu died, his two sons Fonu and Fogou fled to Guanzhong; Fu Jian made Fonu Right General and Fogou Protector-General Who Pacifies the Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After Songnu's death his sons Fonu and Fogou fled to Guanzhong; Fu Jian made Fonu Right General and Fogou Protector-General Who Pacifies the Yi.

sentences.zh: 後以女妻佛奴子定，以定為尚書、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he gave his daughter in marriage to Fonu's son Ding and appointed Ding Minister of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He later married his daughter to Fonu's son Ding and made Ding Minister of the Masters of Writing and General-in-Chief of the Army.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝太元八年，苻堅敗於淮南，關中擾亂，定盡力奉堅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taixuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Fu Jian was defeated at Huainan; Guanzhong was thrown into turmoil, and Ding did all he could to support Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taixuan (383), after Fu Jian's defeat at Feishui, Guanzhong fell into chaos and Ding did everything he could to support him.

sentences.zh: 堅死，乃將家奔隴右，徙治歷城，城在西縣界，去仇池百二十里。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Ding then led his household to flee to Longyou, moved his seat to Licheng—the city lay on the border of Xi County, one hundred twenty li from Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian's death Ding fled with his family to Longyou and made Licheng his capital; the town stood in Xi County, a hundred twenty li from Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 置倉儲於百頃。

translations.literal: He established granaries at Hundred Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He set up granaries at Hundred Qing.

sentences.zh: 招合夷、晉，得千餘家，自號龍驤將軍、平羌校尉、仇池公，稱蕃於晉孝武帝，孝武帝即以其自號假之。

translations.literal: He gathered Yi and Jin households and obtained more than a thousand families; he styled himself Dragon-Prancing General, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi, declared himself a vassal of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, and Xiaowu provisionally granted him those self-assumed titles.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied Yi and Han settlers into more than a thousand households, took the titles Dragon-Prancing General, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi, submitted to Emperor Xiaowu, who confirmed those self-chosen titles.

sentences.zh: 求割天水之西縣、武都之上祿為仇池郡，見許。

translations.literal: He requested that Xi County of Tianshui and Shanglu of Wudu be carved out as the commandery of Chouchi; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Xi County in Tianshui and Shanglu in Wudu be carved out as Chouchi commandery, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十五年，又以定為輔國將軍、秦州刺史，定已自署征西將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Ding was again made General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Qin Province; Ding had already on his own authority styled himself General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Ding was named General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Qin, though he had already styled himself General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 又進持節、都督隴右諸軍事、輔國大將軍、開府儀同三司，校尉、刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Longyou, Grand General Who Assists the State, and Bearer of the Golden Ax with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Excellencies; his colonel and inspector titles remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of Longyou forces, Grand General Who Assists the State, and ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, while keeping his colonel and inspector posts.

sentences.zh: 其年，進平天水略陽郡，遂有秦州之地，自號隴西王。

translations.literal: That same year he advanced and pacified the commanderies of Tianshui and Lueyang, thereby holding the territory of Qin Province, and styled himself King of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: That year he conquered Tianshui and Lueyang and held Qin Province, styling himself King of Longxi.

sentences.zh: [5]至十九年，攻隴西虜乞佛乾歸，定軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: [5]By the nineteenth year he attacked the Longxi barbarian Qifu Gangui; Ding's army was defeated and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: [5]By the nineteenth year (394) he attacked the Longxi ruler Qifu Gangui; Ding's army was routed and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 無子，佛狗子盛先為監國，守仇池，襲位，自號使持節、征西將軍、秦州刺史、平羌校尉、仇池公。

translations.literal: Having no son, Fogou's son Sheng had earlier served as overseer of the state and guarded Chouchi; he succeeded to the position and styled himself Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Qin Province, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he was succeeded by Fogou's son Sheng, who had been regent at Chouchi; Sheng took the titles Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Qin, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 諡定為武王。

translations.literal: Ding was given the posthumous title Martial King.
translations.idiomatic: Ding received the posthumous title Martial King.

sentences.zh: 分諸四山氐、羌為二十部護軍，各為鎮戍，不置郡縣。

translations.literal: He divided the Di and Qiang of the four mountains into twenty divisions of Protector-Generals, each garrisoned in place, and did not establish commanderies or counties.
translations.idiomatic: He split the Di and Qiang of the four mountains into twenty garrison commands, each with its own post, and dispensed with regular prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 安帝隆安三年，遣使稱蕃，奉獻方物。

translations.literal: In the third year of Long'an under Emperor An he sent envoys to declare himself a vassal and presented local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Long'an (399) he sent envoys to submit tribute.

sentences.zh: 安帝以盛為輔國將軍、平羌校尉、仇池公。

translations.literal: Emperor An made Sheng General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An appointed Sheng General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 元興三年，桓玄輔晉，進盛平北將軍、涼州刺史、西戎校尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanxing, when Huan Xuan held power in Jin, Sheng was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Liang Province, and Colonel of the Western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanxing (404), while Huan Xuan dominated the Jin court, Sheng was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Liang, and Colonel of the Western Rong.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年，姚興伐盛，盛懼，遣子難當為質。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yixi, Yao Xing attacked Sheng; Sheng was afraid and sent his son Nandang as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yixi (405), Yao Xing attacked him; frightened, Sheng sent his son Nandang as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 興遣將王敏攻城，因梁州別駕呂瑩，求救於盛，盛遣軍次濜口，敏退。

translations.literal: Xing sent the general Wang Min to attack the city; through Liang Province's Vice-Prefect Lu Ying he sought aid from Sheng; Sheng sent troops to encamp at the Jin Ford, and Min withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Wang Min to besiege the city; through Liang's vice-prefect Lu Ying he appealed to Sheng, who marched to the Jin Ford and forced Min to withdraw.

sentences.zh: [6]以盛為都督隴右諸軍事、征西大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: [6]Sheng was made Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Longyou, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and Bearer of the Golden Ax with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: [6]Sheng was named supervisor of Longyou, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and granted ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時益州刺史毛璩討桓玄所置梁州刺史桓希，敗走，漢中空虛，盛遣兄子平南將軍撫守漢中。

translations.literal: At that time Yi Province Inspector Mao Qiu attacked Huan Xi, whom Huan Xuan had installed as Inspector of Liang Province; Mao was defeated and fled, Hanzhong was left empty, and Sheng sent his elder brother's son Fu, General Who Pacifies the South, to hold Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Inspector Mao Qiu had attacked Huan Xuan's appointee Huan Xi in Liang and been routed, leaving Hanzhong undefended; Sheng sent his nephew Fu, General Who Pacifies the South, to occupy it.

sentences.zh: 三年，又假盛使持節、北秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year Sheng was again provisionally made Bearer of the Staff and Inspector of Northern Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was also given Bearer of the Staff and Inspector of Northern Qin.

sentences.zh: 盛又遣將苻宣行梁州刺史代撫。

translations.literal: Sheng also sent the general Fu Xuan to act as Inspector of Liang Province in Fu's place.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then sent Fu Xuan to replace Fu as acting Inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 九年，梁州刺史索邈鎮南城，宣乃還。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Liang Province Inspector Suo Miao garrisoned Nancheng, and Xuan then returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Suo Miao took Nancheng as Liang inspector, and Xuan withdrew.

sentences.zh: [7]高祖踐阼，進盛車騎大將軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: [7]When Gaozu ascended the throne, Sheng was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: [7]When Gaozu took the throne, Sheng was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and made Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，改封武都王，以長子玄為武都王世子，加號前將軍，難當為冠軍將軍，撫為安南將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu his enfeoffment was changed and he was made King of Wudu; his eldest son Xuan was made Heir Apparent of Wudu with the additional title Forward General, Nandang Champion General, and Fu General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu (422) he was enfeoffed as King of Wudu; his eldest son Xuan became heir with the title Forward General, Nandang Champion General, and Fu General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 盛嗣位三十年，太祖元嘉二年六月卒，時年六十二，私諡曰惠文王。

translations.literal: Sheng held the succession for thirty years; in the sixth month of the second year of Yuanjia under Taizu he died, aged sixty-two; his private posthumous title was Cultured and Martial King.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng reigned thirty years and died in the sixth month of the second year of Yuanjia (425), aged sixty-two; his household gave him the posthumous title Cultured and Martial King.

sentences.zh: 玄字黃眉，自號使持節、都督隴右諸軍事、征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、平羌校尉、秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: Xuan, style name Huangmei, styled himself Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Longyou, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Bearer of the Golden Ax with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Excellencies, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Qin Province, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, styled Huangmei, took the full titles Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of Longyou, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Qin, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 雖為蕃臣，猶奉義熙之號。

translations.literal: Although a vassal prince, he still used the reign title Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: Though a vassal, he still dated documents to the Yixi era.

sentences.zh: 善待士，為流、舊所懷。

translations.literal: He treated scholars well and was cherished by refugees and old retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He treated scholars generously and won the loyalty of refugees and longtime followers.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍撫有文武智略，玄不能容，三年，因其子殺人，并誅之。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Fu had both civil and military talent and stratagem; Xuan could not tolerate him; in the third year, on the pretext that Fu's son had committed murder, he executed Fu as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, General Who Pacifies the South, was gifted in civil and military affairs, which Xuan could not abide; in the third year he used Fu's son's homicide as a pretext to execute Fu too.

sentences.zh: 太祖即以玄為使持節、征西將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: Taizu thereupon appointed Xuan Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin Province, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then confirmed Xuan as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: [8]乃改義熙之號，奉元嘉正朔。

translations.literal: [8]He then changed from the Yixi reign title and adopted the calendar of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: [8]He then abandoned the Yixi era and adopted the Yuanjia calendar.

sentences.zh: 初，盛謂玄曰：「吾年已老，當為晉臣，汝善事宋帝。

translations.literal: Earlier Sheng had told Xuan: "I am already old and shall remain a subject of Jin; you must serve the Emperor of Song well."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had once told Xuan, "I am old and will die a subject of Jin; you must serve the Song emperor faithfully."

sentences.zh: 」故玄奉焉。

translations.literal: " Therefore Xuan followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Xuan did as he had been told.

sentences.zh: 追贈盛驃騎大將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: Sheng was posthumously enfeoffed as Cavalry General-in-Chief; his other titles remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was posthumously made Cavalry General-in-Chief; his other honors stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，玄卒，私諡曰孝昭王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year Xuan died; his private posthumous title was Filial and Illustrious King.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan died in the sixth month of the sixth year (429); his household gave him the posthumous title Filial and Illustrious King.

sentences.zh: 弟難當廢玄子保宗一名羌奴而自立，號使持節、都督雍涼諸軍事、秦州刺史、平羌校尉、武都王。

translations.literal: His younger brother Nandang deposed Xuan's son Baozong—also named Qiangnu—and installed himself, styling himself Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Yong and Liang, Inspector of Qin Province, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Nandang deposed Xuan's son Baozong (also called Qiangnu) and seized power as Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of Yong and Liang, Inspector of Qin, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 太祖以為冠軍將軍、秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: Taizu appointed him Champion General, Inspector of Qin Province, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu recognized him as Champion General, Inspector of Qin, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 九年，進號征西將軍，加持節、都督、校尉之號。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West, with the staff, supervisory, and colonel titles added.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West, retaining Bearer of the Staff, supervisory command, and colonel titles.

sentences.zh: 難當拜保宗為鎮南將軍，鎮宕昌，以次子順為鎮東將軍、秦州刺史，守上邽。

translations.literal: Nandang appointed Baozong General Who Guards the South and garrisoned Dangchang; he made his second son Shun General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qin Province to hold Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang made Baozong General Who Guards the South at Dangchang and his second son Shun General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qin at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 保宗謀襲難當，事泄，收繫之。

translations.literal: Baozong plotted to attack Nandang by surprise; the affair was exposed and he was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Baozong plotted against Nandang; the plot leaked and he was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 先是，四方流民有許穆之、郝恢之二人投難當，並改姓為司馬。

translations.literal: Earlier, among refugees from all quarters there were two men, Xu Muzhi and Hao Huizhi, who came to Nandang and both changed their surnames to Sima.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier two refugees, Xu Muzhi and Hao Huizhi, had come to Nandang and both adopted the surname Sima.

sentences.zh: 穆之自云名飛龍，恢之自云名康之，云是晉室近戚。

translations.literal: Muzhi claimed his name was Feilong, Huizhi claimed his name was Kangzhi, and they said they were close kin of the house of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi called himself Feilong, Huizhi Kangzhi, and both claimed to be near kin of the Jin imperial house.

sentences.zh: 康之尋為人所殺。

translations.literal: Kangzhi was soon killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhi was soon murdered.

sentences.zh: 十年，難當以益州刺史劉道濟失蜀土人情，以兵力資飛龍，使入蜀為寇，道濟擊斬之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Nandang, because Yi Province Inspector Liu Daoji had lost the hearts of the people of Shu, supplied Feilong with troops and sent him into Shu as a raider; Daoji attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (433), seeing that Liu Daoji had lost the loyalty of Shu, Nandang armed Feilong and sent him to raid the province; Daoji defeated and executed him.

sentences.zh: 時梁州刺史甄法護刑法不理，太祖遣刺史蕭思話代任。

translations.literal: At that time Liang Province Inspector Zhen Fahu did not administer penal law properly; Taizu sent Inspector Xiao Sihua to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Inspector Zhen Fahu governed harshly and unjustly, so Taizu sent Xiao Sihua to replace him.

sentences.zh: 難當因思話未至，法護將下，[9]舉兵襲梁州，破白馬，獲晉昌太守張範。

translations.literal: Nandang, because Sihua had not yet arrived and Fahu was about to step down,[9] raised troops and struck Liang Province, broke through Baima, and captured Jinchang Administrator Zhang Fan.
translations.idiomatic: While Sihua was still en route and Fahu about to leave office,[9] Nandang marched into Liang, took Baima, and captured Jinchang prefect Zhang Fan.

sentences.zh: 法護遣參軍魯安期、沈法慧等拒之，並各奔退。

translations.literal: Fahu sent his staff officers Lu Anqi, Shen Fahui, and others to resist, but each fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu sent staff officers Lu Anqi and Shen Fahui to resist, but they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 難當又遣建忠將軍趙進攻葭萌，獲晉壽太守范延朗。

translations.literal: Nandang also sent the General Who Establishes Loyalty Zhao Jin to attack Jiameng and captured Jinshou Administrator Fan Yanlang.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent General Who Establishes Loyalty Zhao Jin against Jiameng and captured Jinshou prefect Fan Yanlang.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，法護委鎮奔洋川，難當遂有漢中之地。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year Fahu abandoned his post and fled to Yangchuan; Nandang thereby held the territory of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: That November Fahu abandoned his post for Yangchuan, and Nandang held Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 以氐苻粟持為梁州刺史，又以其凶悍殺之，以司馬趙溫代為梁州。

translations.literal: He appointed the Di Fu Suchi Inspector of Liang Province, then because of his fierceness and brutality killed him, and made the Sima Zhao Wen acting Inspector of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He installed the Di leader Fu Suchi as Liang inspector, then killed him for brutality and replaced him with the Sima clansman Zhao Wen.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，思話使司馬蕭承之先驅進討，所向剋捷，遂平梁州，事在思話傳。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year Sihua sent his marshal Xiao Chengzhi as vanguard to advance and attack; wherever he went he was victorious, and Liang Province was thereby pacified—the affair is recorded in Sihua's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year Sihua sent Xiao Chengzhi ahead; Chengzhi won every engagement and recovered Liang—as told in Sihua's biography.

sentences.zh: 四月，難當遣使奉表謝罪，曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month Nandang sent envoys presenting a memorial to confess guilt, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Nandang sent envoys with a memorial of apology, which read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞生成之德，含氣同係，而榮悴殊塗，遭遇異兆，至於恩降自然，誠無答謝。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the virtue of engendering life binds all who breathe qi in one lineage, yet glory and decline follow different paths and encounters bring unlike omens; as for grace descending of itself, there is truly no way to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the grace that gives life binds all living things, yet fortune and ruin take different roads and fate deals unequal lots; when favor descends unbidden, no thanks can ever suffice.

sentences.zh: 夫以狂聖道隔，猶存克念之誠，況君親莫二，不期自感者哉。

translations.literal: Even when the way of the mad and the sage stands apart, the resolve to restrain one's thoughts may still remain—how much more when lord and parent are without a second, should one not be moved of itself?
translations.idiomatic: Even madmen and sages are divided by the Way, yet restraint of heart may remain—how much more when sovereign and father are one, should gratitude not arise unbidden?

sentences.zh: 每思自竭，奉遵光訓，丹誠未諒，大謗已臻。

translations.literal: Whenever I think to exhaust myself in service and follow your luminous instruction, my crimson sincerity has not yet been understood and great slander has already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Though I strive to obey your enlightened command, my loyal heart has not been believed and grave calumny has already fallen upon me.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史甄法護誣臣遣司馬飛龍擾亂西蜀，諸所譖引，言非一事，長塗萬里，無路自明，風塵之聲，日有滋甚。

translations.literal: Liang Province Inspector Zhen Fahu slandered your subject, alleging that I sent the Sima Feilong to disturb western Shu; the various accusations cited were not of a single kind; ten thousand li on the long road—there was no way to clear myself, and rumors in the wind grew daily more severe.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Inspector Zhen Fahu accused me of sending the Sima Feilong to ravage western Shu; the charges multiplied, and across ten thousand li I had no means to clear my name while slander spread ever thicker.

sentences.zh: 與其逆生，寧就清滅，文武同憤，制不自由。

translations.literal: Rather than live against your will, I would rather accept clear extinction; civil and military officers shared the same indignation and could not restrain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than live in defiance of your will, we would accept destruction; my civil and military officers burned with the same anger and could not be held back.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍姚道賢齎書詣梁州刺史蕭思話，尋續又遣詣臺歸罪。

translations.literal: I sent Staff Officer Yao Daoxian bearing a letter to Liang Province Inspector Xiao Sihua, and soon after sent another to the capital to confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I sent Staff Officer Yao Daoxian with a letter to Xiao Sihua in Liang, and soon after another envoy to the capital to submit to judgment.

sentences.zh: 道賢至西城，為守兵所殺，行李蔽擁，日月莫照。

translations.literal: Daoxian reached Xicheng and was killed by the garrison troops; his baggage was seized and blocked off, and sun and moon could not shine upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxian reached Xicheng and was killed by the garrison; his escort was seized and his plea never reached the light of day.

sentences.zh: 法護恇擾，望風奔逃，臣即回軍，秋毫無犯，權留少守，以俟會通。

translations.literal: Fahu was alarmed and fled at the sight of our banners; your subject then withdrew the army without violating so much as an autumn hair, leaving only a small garrison provisionally to await restored communication.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu panicked and fled at our approach; I withdrew without harming a thing, leaving only a small guard to await your orders.

sentences.zh: 其後數旬，官軍尋至，守兵單弱，懼不自免，續遣輕兵，共相迎接。

translations.literal: Several tens of days later the government army arrived; the garrison was few and weak, fearing they could not escape, and again sent light troops to welcome one another.
translations.idiomatic: Weeks later imperial troops arrived; our thin garrison feared it could not survive and sent light units out to greet them.

sentences.zh: 值秦流民，懷土及本，行將既旋，不容禁制，由臣約防無素，以致斯闕。

translations.literal: We encountered Qin refugees who longed for their native soil; as the army was about to turn back they could not be restrained—because your subject's discipline and defenses had been lax, this fault arose.
translations.idiomatic: We met Qin refugees homesick for their native land; as our columns turned homeward they could not be restrained—through my lax discipline this breach occurred.

sentences.zh: 臣本歷代守蕃，世荷殊寵，王化始基，順天委命，要名期義，不在今日，豈可假託妖妄，毀敗成功，如此之形，灼然易見，仰恃聖明，必垂鑒察。

translations.literal: Your subject's family has for generations guarded the frontier and received extraordinary favor; as royal transformation first took foundation I submitted to Heaven and entrusted my fate—seeking reputation and expecting righteousness was not for today; how could I borrow false pretexts of demonic delusion to ruin accomplished success? Such a shape is plainly easy to see; relying on your sagely clarity, it will surely receive scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: My house has guarded the frontier for generations under exceptional grace; when your rule first took root I submitted to Heaven's mandate—my quest for honor was never for this day alone. How could I cloak myself in false rebellion to ruin what we have built? The truth is obvious; I trust your sage discernment will see it.

sentences.zh: 但臣微心不達，迹違忠順，至乃聲聞朝庭，勞煩師旅，負辱之深，罪當誅責。

translations.literal: Yet your subject's slight heart did not penetrate, my tracks departed from loyalty and obedience, until the report reached the court and troubled the armies—the burden of shame is deep; the crime deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my humble intent failed to reach you; my actions seemed disloyal until the court heard of them and armies were set in motion. The shame is overwhelming, and the fault deserves death.

sentences.zh: 遠隔遐荒，告謝無地，謹遣兼長史齊亮聽命有司，并奉送所授第十一符策，伏待天旨。

translations.literal: Far separated in distant wilds, there is no place to declare thanks; I respectfully send Acting Chief Clerk Qi Liang to await orders from the authorities, and together present the eleventh tally and patent bestowed upon me, prostrate awaiting Heaven's decree.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off in distant borderlands, I have no means to plead in person; I send Acting Chief Clerk Qi Liang to await your officials' command and return the eleventh tally and patent you granted, bowing until your decree arrives.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其邊裔，下詔曰：「楊難當表如此，悔謝前愆，可特恕宥，并特還章節。」

translations.literal: Taizu, because he was a border subject, issued an edict saying: "Yang Nandang's memorial is thus; regretting and apologizing for past faults, he may be specially pardoned and forgiven, and his seals and credentials are specially to be returned."
translations.idiomatic: Because he was a frontier vassal, Taizu issued an edict: "Nandang's memorial shows repentance for past offenses; he is specially pardoned, and his seals and insignia are to be returned."

sentences.zh: 十二年，難當釋保宗，遣鎮童亭，[10]保宗奔，[11]索虜主拓跋燾以為都督隴西諸軍事、征西大將軍、開府儀同三司、平羌校尉、南秦王，遣襲上邽，難當子順失守退，以為雍州刺史，守下辯。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Nandang released Baozong and sent him to garrison Tongting;[10] Baozong fled;[11] the Suo Lu ruler Tuoba Tao appointed him Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Longxi, General Who Conquers the West, Cap and Sword Equal to the Three Ministers, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and King of Southern Qin, and sent him to raid Shanggui; Nandang's son Shun lost his defense and withdrew, and was made Inspector of Yong Province to hold Xiabian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Nandang freed Baozong and posted him at Tongting;[10] Baozong defected;[11] the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao made him commander of Longxi, General Who Conquers the West, with full ceremonial honors, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and King of Southern Qin, and sent him against Shanggui. Nandang's son Shun abandoned his post; Tuoba made him Yong inspector at Xiabian.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，難當自立為大秦王，號年曰建義，立妻為王后，世子為太子，置百官，具擬天朝，然猶奉朝庭，貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year Nandang set himself up as Great King of Qin, styled his reign era Jianyi, made his wife queen, his heir crown prince, established the hundred offices—all fully modeled on the imperial court—yet he still submitted to the court, and tribute never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year Nandang declared himself Great King of Qin, took the era name Jianyi, crowned his wife and heir, and staffed a full bureaucracy on the imperial model—yet he still paid homage to the Song court and kept sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 十七年，其國大旱，多災異，降大秦王復為武都王。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year his state suffered great drought and many portents; he demoted himself from Great King of Qin back to King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year drought and omens afflicted his realm, and he demoted himself from Great King of Qin to King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 十八年十月，傾國南寇，規有蜀土，慮漢中軍出，遣建忠將軍苻沖出東洛以防之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year he mobilized the whole state to raid south, intending to seize Shu territory; fearing that Hanzhong armies would sortie, he sent the General Who Establishes Loyalty Fu Chong out from Dongluo to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year he hurled his entire kingdom south toward Shu, and sent General Who Establishes Loyalty Fu Chong from Dongluo to block any Hanzhong relief force.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史劉真道擊斬沖。

translations.literal: Liang Province Inspector Liu Zhendao attacked and beheaded Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Inspector Liu Zhendao attacked and killed Chong.

sentences.zh: [12]十一月，難當剋葭萌，獲晉壽太守申坦，遂圍涪城，巴西太守劉道錫嬰城固守，[13]難當攻之十餘日，不剋，乃還。

translations.literal: [12]In the eleventh month Nandang took Jiameng and captured Jinshou Administrator Shen Tan, then besieged Fucheng; Brazil Administrator Liu Daoxi closed the city and held fast;[13] Nandang attacked for more than ten days without taking it, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: [12]In the eleventh month Nandang took Jiameng and captured Jinshou prefect Shen Tan, then laid siege to Fucheng; Brazil prefect Liu Daoxi held the walls;[13] after ten days of assault Nandang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，太祖遣龍驤將軍裴方明、太子左積弩將軍劉康祖、後軍參軍梁坦甲士三千人，又發荊、雍二州兵討難當，受劉真道節度。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year Taizu sent Dragon-Striking General Pei Fangming, the crown prince's Left Stacked-Bolt General Liu Kangzu, and Rear Army Staff Officer Liang Tan with three thousand armored troops, and also raised troops from Jing and Yong Provinces to campaign against Nandang, all under Liu Zhendao's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the nineteenth year Taizu dispatched Pei Fangming as Dragon-Striking General, Liu Kangzu as the crown prince's Left Stacked-Bolt General, and Liang Tan as rear-army staff officer with three thousand armored men, plus armies from Jing and Yong, all under Liu Zhendao's orders against Nandang.

sentences.zh: 五月，方明等至漢中，長驅而進。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Fangming and the others reached Hanzhong and advanced at full speed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Fangming reached Hanzhong and pressed forward without pause.

sentences.zh: 真道到武興，攻偽建忠將軍苻隆，剋之。

translations.literal: Zhendao reached Wuxing, attacked the false General Who Establishes Loyalty Fu Long, and took him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendao reached Wuxing and defeated the rebel General Who Establishes Loyalty Fu Long.

sentences.zh: 安西參軍韋俊、建武將軍姜道盛別向下辯，真道又遣司馬夏侯穆季西取白水，難當子雍州刺史順、建忠將軍楊亮拒之，並望風奔走。

translations.literal: Anxi Staff Officer Wei Jun and the General Who Establishes Martial Might Jiang Daosheng separately advanced toward Xiabian; Zhendao also sent Marshal Xiahou Mu seasonally west to take Baishui; Nandang's son Yong Inspector Shun and General Who Establishes Loyalty Yang Liang resisted them, but both fled at sight of the banners.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer Wei Jun and General Who Establishes Martial Might Jiang Daosheng marched on Xiabian while Zhendao sent Marshal Xiahou Mu west to Baishui; Nandang's son Shun, Yong inspector, and General Who Establishes Loyalty Yang Liang both fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 閏月，方明至蘭臯，難當鎮北將軍苻義德、建節將軍苻弘祖萬餘人列陣拒戰，方明擊破之，斬弘祖，殺二千餘人，義德遁去。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Fangming reached Lan'gao; Nandang's General Who Guards the North Fu Yide and Commissioner-General Fu Hongzu arrayed more than ten thousand men to resist; Fangming broke them, beheaded Hongzu, killed more than two thousand, and Yide fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month at Lan'gao, Fu Yide and Fu Hongzu fielded over ten thousand men; Fangming routed them, killed Hongzu and two thousand soldiers, and Yide escaped.

sentences.zh: 天水任愈之率部曲歸順。

translations.literal: Tianshui's Ren Yuzhi led his private troops to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuzhi of Tianshui led his followers in surrender.

sentences.zh: 難當世子撫軍大將軍和據修城，方明又遣軍率愈之攻和，大破之。

translations.literal: Nandang's heir, General Who Assists the Army He, held Xiucheng; Fangming again sent troops with Yuzhi to attack He and utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang's heir He, General Who Assists the Army, held Xiucheng; Fangming sent Yuzhi against him and crushed his force.

sentences.zh: 於是難當將妻子奔索虜，死于虜中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nandang took wife and children and fled to the Suo Lu; he died among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang then fled with his family to the Northern Wei and died in their lands.

sentences.zh: 安西參軍魯尚期追難當出寒峽，[14]生禽建節將軍楊保熾、安昌侯楊虎頭。

translations.literal: Anxi Staff Officer Lu Shangqi pursued Nandang out through Han Gorge;[14] he captured alive Commissioner-General Yang Baoju and Marquis of Anchang Yang Hutou.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer Lu Shangqi pursued Nandang through Han Gorge[14] and took alive Commissioner-General Yang Baoju and Marquis of Anchang Yang Hutou.

sentences.zh: 初，難當遣第二子虎為鎮南將軍、益州刺史，守陰平。

translations.literal: Earlier Nandang had sent his second son Hu as General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Yi Province to hold Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Nandang had posted his second son Hu as General Who Guards the South and Yi inspector at Yinping.

sentences.zh: 聞父走，逃還，至下辯。

translations.literal: Hearing that his father had fled, he escaped back and reached Xiabian.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of his father's flight, Hu fled back to Xiabian.

sentences.zh: 方明使子肅之要之，生禽虎，傳送京師，斬于建康市。

translations.literal: Fangming sent his son Suzhi to intercept him, captured Hu alive, sent him to the capital, and executed him in the Jiankang marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming sent his son Suzhi to cut him off, captured Hu, sent him to the capital, and had him beheaded in the Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 仇池平。

translations.literal: Chouchi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chouchi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 以輔國司馬胡崇之為龍驤將軍、秦州刺史、平羌校尉，守仇池。

translations.literal: Assistant-to-the-State Marshal Hu Chongzhi was made Dragon-Striking General, Inspector of Qin Province, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, to guard Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chongzhi, assistant-to-the-state marshal, was appointed Dragon-Striking General, Qin inspector, and Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang to hold Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 索虜拓跋燾遣安西大將軍吐奚弼、平北將軍拓跋齊等二萬人邀崇之。

translations.literal: The Suo Lu Tuoba Tao sent Anxi Grand General Tuxi Bi, General Who Pacifies the North Tuoba Qi, and others—twenty thousand men—to intercept Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Tao of the Northern Wei sent Anxi Grand General Tuxi Bi and General Who Pacifies the North Tuoba Qi with twenty thousand men to ambush Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 二十年二月，崇之至濁水，去仇池八十里，遇齊等，戰敗沒，餘眾奔還漢中。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twentieth year Chongzhi reached Zhuoshui, eighty li from Chouchi, encountered Qi and the others, was defeated and perished, and the remnant troops fled back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twentieth year Chongzhi reached Zhuoshui, eighty li from Chouchi, met Qi, was defeated and killed, and the survivors fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 三月，前鎮東司馬苻達、征西從事中郎任朏等舉義，立保宗弟文德為主。

translations.literal: In the third month the former Marshal of the East Fu Da, Western Campaign Attendant-of-the-Staff Ren Fei, and others raised a righteous rising and installed Baozong's younger brother Wende as lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month former eastern marshal Fu Da, staff officer Ren Fei, and others rebelled and set up Baozong's brother Wende as their leader.

sentences.zh: 拓跋齊聞兵起遁走，達追擊斬齊，[15]因據白崖，分平諸戍。

translations.literal: Tuoba Qi, hearing that troops had risen, fled; Da pursued, attacked, and beheaded Qi;[15] they then seized Baiya and in detachments pacified the various garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Qi fled at news of the uprising; Da pursued and killed him;[15] they took Baiya and pacified the outlying garrisons.

sentences.zh: 文德自號使持節、都督秦河涼三州諸軍事、征西大將軍、秦河涼三州牧、平羌校尉、仇池公，遣露板馳告朝廷。

translations.literal: Wende styled himself Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Qin, He, and Liang, General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Qin, He, and Liang, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi, and sent an open proclamation swiftly to inform the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wende took the titles Bearer of the Staff, commander of Qin, He, and Liang, General Who Conquers the West, governor of those three provinces, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Duke of Chouchi, and sent an open bulletin to the court.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔曰：「近者校尉仇池公表虜縱逸，寇竊仇池，將士挫傷，民萌塗炭，眷言四顧，矜慨在懷。

translations.literal: Taizu issued an edict saying: "Recently Colonel Duke of Chouchi memorialized that the barbarians ran wild, raided and stole Chouchi, soldiers were wounded and defeated, and the people were scorched—looking about on every side, compassion and indignation fill the breast."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu decreed: "The Duke of Chouchi recently reported that the barbarians ran amok, seized Chouchi, wounded our troops, and ravaged the people—my heart turns in grief and anger on every side."

sentences.zh: 楊文德世篤忠順，誠感家國，糾率義徒，奄殄凶醜，鋒旗所向，殲潰無遺，氛祲澄清，蕃境寧一，念功惟事，良有欣嘉。

translations.literal: Yang Wende for generations has been deeply loyal and obedient; his sincerity moves state and family; he gathered righteous followers and swiftly extinguished the vicious foe; wherever his banners pointed, none escaped annihilation; the baleful mists cleared, the frontier was unified in peace—considering his merit alone, there is indeed cause for joy and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wende's house has long been steadfastly loyal; moved by devotion to the realm, he rallied righteous followers and swiftly destroyed the enemy; his banners left no foe standing, the frontier mists cleared, and the borderlands were pacified—his merit gives me true joy.

sentences.zh: 便可遣使慰勞，宣示朝旨，并勑梁州刺史申坦隨宜應援。

translations.literal: Envoys may now be sent to comfort and encourage him, proclaim the court's intent, and also command Liang Province Inspector Shen Tan to support him as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to comfort him, proclaim the court's will, and order Liang Inspector Shen Tan to aid him as needed.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「顯錄勳効，蓋惟國典，施賞務速，無或踰時。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "To display and record meritorious achievement is the state's canon; bestowing rewards must be swift and must not exceed the proper season."
translations.idiomatic: " Another edict read: "Recording merit is the law of the state; rewards must be swift and never delayed."

sentences.zh: 楊文德志氣果到，文武兼全，乘機潛奮，殊功仍集，告捷歸誠，獻俘萬里，朝無暫土，樹難自肅，休烈昭著，朕甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: Yang Wende's will and spirit are resolute and penetrating; civil and military talents are complete; seizing the moment he secretly exerted himself and extraordinary merit accumulated; reporting victory he returned in loyalty, presenting captives across ten thousand li; the court had not a moment's delay in granting land; troubles in the trees self-subdued; his splendid achievements are manifest—I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wende is resolute in spirit and master of both civil and military arts; seizing his chance he won signal victories, reported triumph, and offered captives from afar; without delay the court granted him domain and his enemies fell away—his splendid deeds shine forth, and I greatly commend them.

sentences.zh: 楊氏世祖西勞，方忠累葉，[16]宜紹先緒，膺受寵榮。

translations.literal: The Yang clan's forebears toiled in the west; loyalty has piled up generation upon generation;[16] he should continue the former line and receive favor and glory.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang house toiled on the western frontier through generations of loyalty;[16] he should inherit their line and receive imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 可使持節、散騎常侍、都督北秦雍二州諸軍事、征西大將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史，封武都王。

translations.literal: He may be made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Northern Qin and Yong, General Who Conquers the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin Province, and enfeoffed as King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, commander of Northern Qin and Yong, General Who Conquers the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Northern Qin inspector, and enfeoffed as King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 」任朏祖父岐，伯父祚，父綜，並仕楊氏，為諮議從事中郎。

translations.literal: " Ren Fei's grandfather Qi, his father's elder brother Zuo, and his father Zong all served the Yang clan as Advisory Attendants-of-the-Staff.
translations.idiomatic: " Ren Fei's grandfather Qi, uncle Zuo, and father Zong had all served the Yang as advisory staff officers.

sentences.zh: 朏有志幹，文德以為左司馬。

translations.literal: Fei had will and capacity; Wende made him Left Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was capable and resolute; Wende appointed him Left Marshal.

sentences.zh: 文德既受朝命，進戍茄蘆城。

translations.literal: Once Wende had received the court's commission, he advanced to garrison Qielu City.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the court's commission, Wende advanced to garrison Qielu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，為索虜所攻，奔于漢中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was attacked by the Suo Lu and fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Northern Wei attacked him and he fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時世祖鎮襄陽，執文德歸之于京師，以失守，免官，削爵土。

translations.literal: At that time Shizu was garrisoning Xiangyang; he seized Wende and sent him back to the capital; for losing his post he was dismissed from office and stripped of title and fief.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, then garrisoning Xiangyang, seized Wende and sent him to the capital; for losing his territory he was dismissed and stripped of rank and lands.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，王師北討，起文德為輔國將軍，率軍自漢中西入，搖動汧、隴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the royal army campaigned north; Wende was raised as General Who Assists the State and led troops west from Hanzhong, shaking Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, during the northern campaign, Wende was recalled as General Who Assists the State and led troops west from Hanzhong to stir unrest in Qian and Long.

sentences.zh: 文德宗人楊高率陰平、平武羣氐，據唐魯橋以距文德，文德水陸俱攻，大破之，眾並奔散。

translations.literal: Wende's clansman Yang Gao led the Di clans of Yinping and Pingwu, held Tanglu Bridge to resist Wende; Wende attacked by land and water together and utterly defeated them; the masses all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Wende's kinsman Yang Gao rallied the Di of Yinping and Pingwu at Tanglu Bridge; Wende attacked by land and river, routed them, and their followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 高遁走奔羌，文德追之至黎卬嶺，高單身投羌仇阿弱家，追斬之，陰平、平武悉平。

translations.literal: Gao fled and ran to the Qiang; Wende pursued him to Liyang Ridge; Gao alone threw himself on the Qiang Chou Arouo's household; he was pursued and beheaded; Yinping and Pingwu were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Gao fled among the Qiang; Wende pursued him to Liyang Ridge, where Gao alone sought refuge with the Qiang leader Chou Arouo; Wende caught and killed him, and Yinping and Pingwu were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 又遣文德伐啖提氐，不剋，梁州刺史劉秀之執送荊州，使文德從祖兄頭戍茄蘆。

translations.literal: He again sent Wende to campaign against the Danti Di but he did not prevail; Liang Province Inspector Liu Xiuzhi seized him and sent him to Jing Province, and made Wende's father's cousin Tou garrison Qielu.
translations.idiomatic: Wende was sent against the Danti Di but failed; Liang Inspector Liu Xiuzhi arrested him and sent him to Jing, posting Wende's cousin Tou at Qielu.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史南郡王義宣反，文德不同見殺，世祖追贈征虜將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Jing Province Inspector the Prince of Nanjun Yixuan rebelled; Wende would not join him and was killed; Shizu posthumously enfeoffed him as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjun Prince Yixuan rebelled as Jing inspector, Wende refused to follow and was executed; Shizu posthumously granted him General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Qin inspector.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，以保宗子元和為征虜將軍，以頭為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, Baozong's son Yuanhe was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and Tou was made General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian, Baozong's son Yuanhe became General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Tou General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 元和既楊氏正統，羣氐欲相宗推，年小才弱，不能綏御所部，頭母妻子弟並為索虜所執，頭至誠奉順，無所顧懷。

translations.literal: Yuanhe being the Yang clan's legitimate line, the Di clans wished to honor and elevate one another; he was young and his talent weak, unable to pacify and control his command; Tou's mother, wife, sons, and younger brothers were all seized by the Suo Lu, yet Tou with utmost sincerity submitted and obeyed, without any regard for personal concerns.
translations.idiomatic: As the legitimate Yang heir, Yuanhe was whom the Di wished to follow, but he was young and weak and could not govern his people; the Northern Wei had seized Tou's mother, wife, children, and brothers, yet Tou remained utterly loyal without thought for his family.

sentences.zh: 朝廷既不正元和號位，部落未有定主，雍州刺史王玄謨上表曰：[17]「被勑令臣遣使與楊元和、楊頭相聞，并致信餉。

translations.literal: The court had not yet regularized Yuanhe's title and rank, and the tribes had no settled lord; Yong Province Inspector Wang Xuanmo submitted a memorial saying:[17] "I was commanded to send envoys to communicate with Yang Yuanhe and Yang Tou and also to deliver letters and gifts."
translations.idiomatic: The court had not yet confirmed Yuanhe's status, and the tribes lacked a settled leader; Yong Inspector Wang Xuanmo memorialized:[17] "I was ordered to send envoys to Yang Yuanhe and Yang Tou with letters and gifts."

sentences.zh: 既遣中軍行參軍呂智宗齎書并信等，亦自遣使隨智宗。

translations.literal: I have already sent Central Army Acting Staff Officer Lü Zhizong bearing the letters and gifts and the like, and also sent my own envoy to accompany Zhizong.
translations.idiomatic: I sent Central Army staff officer Lü Zhizong with the letters and gifts, and dispatched my own envoy with him.

sentences.zh: 及頭語智宗，頃破家為國，母妻子弟并墜沒虜中，不顧孝道，陳力邊捍，竭忠盡誠，未為朝廷所識。

translations.literal: When Tou spoke to Zhizong, he said that recently he had broken his family for the state; mother, wife, sons, and younger brothers had all fallen captive among the barbarians; disregarding filial duty he displayed his strength on the frontier defense, exhausting loyalty and utmost sincerity—yet he had not been recognized by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Tou told Zhizong that he had lately ruined his family for the state: his mother, wife, children, and brothers were all captives of the barbarians; abandoning filial duty he served on the frontier with complete loyalty—yet the court had not acknowledged him.

sentences.zh: 若以元和承統，宜授王爵；

translations.literal: If Yuanhe is to succeed to the line, he should be granted a royal title;
translations.idiomatic: If Yuanhe is to inherit the line, he should receive a princely title;

sentences.zh: 若以其年小未堪大任，則應別有所委。

translations.literal: if because he is young and not yet fit for a great charge, then another should be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: if he is too young for great responsibility, another should be appointed.

sentences.zh: 頃來公私紛紜，華、戎交構，皆此之由。

translations.literal: Recently public and private affairs have been tangled, Chinese and barbarians have clashed in mutual intrigue—all from this cause.
translations.idiomatic: The recent turmoil between Chinese and tribes stems entirely from this uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 臣伏尋頭元嘉以來，實有忠誠於國，棄親遺愛，誠在可嘉。

translations.literal: Your subject, bowing in reflection, finds that since Yuanjia Tou has truly been loyal to the state, abandoning kin and leaving behind affection—his sincerity is indeed praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reflection, since the Yuanjia era Tou has shown true loyalty to the state, forsaking family for duty—merit truly worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 氐、羌負遠，又與虜咫尺，急之則反，緩之則怨。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang rely on distance; they are also within a foot's reach of the barbarians—press them and they rebel, ease them and they resent.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang hold remote strongholds yet stand a step from the enemy—press them and they rebel, neglect them and they grow resentful.

sentences.zh: 觀頭使人言語，不敢便望仇池公，所希政在西秦州假節而已。

translations.literal: Observing Tou's envoy's words, he dares not immediately hope for Duke of Chouchi; what he hopes for in governance is only provisional authority in Western Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: From Tou's envoy's words, he does not presume to ask for Duke of Chouchi; he hopes only for provisional authority in Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，蕃捍漢川，使無虜患，頭實有力，四千戶荒州，殆不足吝。

translations.literal: In your subject's foolish view, to guard the frontier and defend Han River lands so that there is no barbarian trouble, Tou truly has strength—a wilderness province of four thousand households is scarcely worth grudging.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, Tou can truly guard Han River lands against the barbarians; a wilderness district of four thousand households is scarcely too much to grant.

sentences.zh: 元和小弱，若未可專委，復數年之後，必堪嗣業，用之不難。

translations.literal: Yuanhe is young and weak; if he cannot yet be solely entrusted, after several more years he will surely be fit to succeed the enterprise—employing him will not be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe is young and weak; if he cannot yet bear sole authority, in a few years he will surely be fit to succeed—then employing him will be easy.

sentences.zh: 若才用不稱，則應歸頭。

translations.literal: If his talent and employment do not match, then authority should revert to Tou.
translations.idiomatic: If his talents prove inadequate, authority should pass to Tou.

sentences.zh: 若茄蘆不守，漢川亦無立理。

translations.literal: If Qielu is not held, Han River lands also have no ground to stand on.
translations.idiomatic: If Qielu cannot be held, the Han River frontier cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 」上不許。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 其後立元和為武都王，治白水，不能自立，復走奔索虜。

translations.literal: Afterward Yuanhe was established as King of Wudu, administering Baishui; he could not stand on his own and again fled and ran to the Suo Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuanhe was made King of Wudu and ruled from Baishui, but could not hold his own and again fled to the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 元和從弟僧嗣，復自立，還戍茄蘆，以為寧朔將軍、仇池太守。

translations.literal: Yuanhe's younger cousin Sengsi again set himself up independently, returned to garrison Qielu, and was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe's cousin Sengsi declared himself leader again, returned to garrison Qielu, and was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Chouchi administrator.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始二年，詔曰：「僧嗣遠守西疆，世篤忠款，宜加旌顯，以甄義概。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Taizong, an edict said: "Sengsi guards the distant western frontier; for generations his loyalty has been deep and sincere—he should receive added commendation and display to distinguish righteous resolve."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi, Taizong decreed: "Sengsi holds the far western frontier; his house has long been steadfastly loyal—he should be honored to mark his righteous spirit."

sentences.zh: 可冠軍將軍、北秦州刺史、武都王，太守如故。

translations.literal: He may be made Champion General, Inspector of Northern Qin Province, King of Wudu—the administrator's post as before.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Champion General, Northern Qin inspector, and King of Wudu, retaining his post as administrator.

sentences.zh: 」三年，加持節、都督北秦雍二州諸軍事，進號征西將軍、校尉，刺史如故。

translations.literal: " In the third year he was given the staff of authority, made Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Northern Qin and Yong, advanced in title to General Who Conquers the West and colonel; inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year he received the staff, command of Northern Qin and Yong, and promotion to General Who Conquers the West and colonel, retaining his inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 僧嗣卒，從弟文度復自立。

translations.literal: Sengsi died; his younger cousin Wendu again set himself up independently.
translations.idiomatic: Sengsi died, and his cousin Wendu declared himself leader again.

sentences.zh: 泰豫元年，以為龍驤將軍、略陽太守，封武都王，又改龍驤為寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyu he was made Dragon-Striking General and Administrator of Lueyang, enfeoffed as King of Wudu, and Dragon-Striking was changed to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiyu he became Dragon-Striking General and Lueyang administrator, was enfeoffed King of Wudu, and his title was changed from Dragon-Striking to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽四年，加督北秦州諸軍事、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, he was additionally made Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Northern Qin, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Inspector of Northern Qin Province; general as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor he was additionally made commander of Northern Qin, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Northern Qin inspector, retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 文度遣弟龍驤將軍文弘伐仇池，[18]破戍兵於蘭臯。

translations.literal: Wendu sent his younger brother Dragon-Striking General Wenhong to campaign against Chouchi;[18] he defeated the garrison troops at Lan'gao.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu sent his brother Wenhong, Dragon-Striking General, against Chouchi;[18] he defeated the garrison at Lan'gao.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明元年，詔曰：「茂賞有章，實昭國度，疇庸斯炳，載宣史冊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, an edict said: "Abundant rewards have their rules—this truly manifests the state's measure; ranking merit thus shines forth and is proclaimed in the historical records."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming, Emperor Shun decreed: "Grand rewards follow clear law, manifesting the state's measure; merit thus shines and is recorded in history."

sentences.zh: 督北秦州諸軍事、寧朔將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史，武都王文度門乘輝寵，世榮邊邑，忠果既亮，才勁兼彰。

translations.literal: Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Northern Qin, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin Province, Wudu King Yang Wendu—his house rides upon brilliant favor; for generations they have been honored on the border towns; loyalty and resolution are already bright; talent and vigor are both manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qin commander, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Northern Qin inspector, King of Wudu Yang Wendu—his house has long enjoyed imperial favor on the frontier; his loyalty is proven and his talent manifest.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍楊文弘肅協成規，躬提桴鼓，申稜百頃，席卷蘭臯，功烈之美，並足嘉歎，宜膺爵授，以酬勳緒。

translations.literal: Dragon-Striking General Yang Wenhong solemnly coordinated to complete the plan, personally raised drum and mallet, extended his edge across a hundred qing, swept up Lan'gao—the beauty of their achievements together suffices for praise and sighing; they should receive enfeoffment and appointment to repay their meritorious line.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-Striking General Yang Wenhong faithfully executed the plan, led the assault in person, swept a hundred qing of ground, and overran Lan'gao—their splendid achievements alike deserve praise; they should receive titles to reward their merit.

sentences.zh: 文度可使持節、都督北秦雍二州諸軍事、征西將軍，刺史、校尉悉如故。

translations.literal: Wendu may be made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Northern Qin and Yong, General Who Conquers the West; inspector and colonel all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu is appointed Bearer of the Staff, commander of Northern Qin and Yong, and General Who Conquers the West, retaining his inspectorship and colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 文弘輔國將軍、略陽太守。

translations.literal: Wenhong: General Who Assists the State, Administrator of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhong: General Who Assists the State and Lueyang administrator.

sentences.zh: 」其年，虜破茄蘆，文度見殺，追贈本官，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " That year the barbarians took Qielu; Wendu was killed; posthumously his former office was granted, with addition of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " That year the barbarians seized Qielu and killed Wendu; he was posthumously granted his former rank plus Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以文弘督北秦州諸軍事、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史，襲封武都王，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Wenhong was made Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Northern Qin, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin Province, succeeding to the enfeoffment as King of Wudu; general as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhong was made commander of Northern Qin, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Northern Qin inspector, and succeeded as King of Wudu, retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 退治武興。

translations.literal: He withdrew to administer Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to rule from Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 大且渠蒙遜，張掖臨松盧水胡人也。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun, Great Chieftain of the Left—was a Lushui Hu man of Lin Song in Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun, the Great Left Chieftain, was a Lushui Hu from Lin Song in Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 匈奴有左且渠、右且渠之官，蒙遜之先為此職，羌之酋豪曰大，故且渠以位為氏，而以大冠之。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu had the offices of Left Chieftain of the Left and Right Chieftain of the Right; Mengxun's forebears held this post; among the Qiang a tribal chieftain is called "great," so Chieftain-of-the-Left became the clan name, with "great" placed before it.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu had Left and Right Chieftain offices; Mengxun's ancestors held them. Qiang chieftains were styled "great," so the clan took Chieftain-of-the-Left as its surname, prefixed with "great."

sentences.zh: 世居盧水為酋豪。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt at Lushui as tribal chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they lived at Lushui as tribal leaders.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜高祖暉仲歸，曾祖遮，皆雄健有勇名。

translations.literal: Mengxun's great-grandfather Huizhonggui, his grandfather Zhe—both were bold and strong with a reputation for courage.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun's great-grandfather Huizhonggui and grandfather Zhe were both famed for strength and valor.

sentences.zh: 祖祁復延，封狄地王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qifu Yan was enfeoffed as King of the Di Lands.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qifu Yan was enfeoffed as King of the Di Lands.

sentences.zh: [19]父法弘襲爵，苻氏以為中田護軍。

translations.literal: [19]His father Fahong succeeded to the title; the Fu clan made him Central Field Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: [19]His father Fahong inherited the title; the Former Qin appointed him Central Field Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜代父領部曲，有勇略，多計數，為諸胡所推服。

translations.literal: Mengxun succeeded his father in leading the private troops; he had courage and stratagem, many schemes, and was pushed forward and submitted to by the various Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun succeeded his father as leader of the tribal forces; bold and resourceful, full of stratagems, he won the allegiance of the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 呂光自王於涼州，使蒙遜自領營人配箱直，又以蒙遜叔父羅仇為西平太守。

translations.literal: Lü Guang made himself king in Liang Province, had Mengxun personally lead his camp followers assigned to box transport duty, and also made Mengxun's uncle Luochou Administrator of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang declared himself king in Liang, he put Mengxun in charge of camp followers on baggage duty and appointed Mengxun's uncle Luochou Xiping administrator.

sentences.zh: [20]安帝隆安三年春，呂光遣子鎮東將軍纂率羅仇伐枹罕虜乞佛乾歸，為乾歸所敗，光委罪羅仇，殺之。

translations.literal: [20]In the spring of the third year of Long'an under Emperor An, Lü Guang sent his son the General Who Guards the East Zuan leading Luochou to campaign against the Fuhan barbarian Qifu Gangui; they were defeated by Gangui; Guang shifted blame to Luochou and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: [20]In the spring of the third year of Long'an (399), Lü Guang sent his son Zuan, General Who Guards the East, with Luochou against the Fuhan leader Qifu Gangui; Gangui defeated them, and Guang blamed Luochou and executed him.

sentences.zh: 四月，蒙遜求還葬羅仇，因聚萬餘人叛光，殺臨松護軍，屯金山。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Mengxun requested to return and bury Luochou; thereby he gathered more than ten thousand men and rebelled against Guang, killed the Protector of the Army at Linsong, and encamped at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Mengxun asked permission to bury Luochou, then rallied more than ten thousand men in revolt against Guang, killed the Linsong garrison commander, and encamped at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 五月，光揮纂擊破蒙遜，蒙遜將六七人，逃山中，[21]家戶悉亡散。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Guang directed Zuan to attack and defeat Mengxun; Mengxun had only six or seven men and fled into the mountains;[21] his household followers all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Guang sent Zuan to rout Mengxun, who escaped into the mountains with only six or seven followers;[21] his household and troops scattered.

sentences.zh: 時蒙遜兄男成將兵西守晉昌，聞蒙遜反，引軍還，殺酒泉太守疊滕，[22]推建康太守段業為主。

translations.literal: At that time Mengxun's elder brother Nancheng was commanding troops guarding Jinchang in the west; hearing that Mengxun had rebelled, he led the army back, killed Jiuquan Administrator Dieteng,[22] and pushed Jianchang Administrator Duan Ye to be lord.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun's elder brother Nancheng was then garrisoning Jinchang in the west; hearing of the revolt, he marched back, killed Jiuquan prefect Dieteng,[22] and installed Jianchang prefect Duan Ye as their leader.

sentences.zh: 業自號龍驤大將軍、涼州牧、建康公，以男成為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Ye styled himself Dragon-Striking Grand General, Governor of Liang Province, Duke of Jianchang, and made Nancheng General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Ye took the titles Dragon-Striking Grand General, Liang governor, and Duke of Jianchang, and made Nancheng General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 男成及晉昌太守王德圍張掖，剋之，業因據張掖。

translations.literal: Nancheng and Jinchang Administrator Wang De besieged Zhangye, took it, and Ye thereby held Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng and Jinchang prefect Wang De besieged and captured Zhangye, which Ye then made his base.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜率部曲投業，業以蒙遜為鎮西將軍、臨池太守，[23]王德為酒泉太守。

translations.literal: Mengxun led his private troops to submit to Ye; Ye made Mengxun General Who Guards the West and Administrator of Linchi,[23] and Wang De Administrator of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun brought his followers to join Ye, who made him General Who Guards the West and Linchi administrator,[23] and Wang De Jiuquan administrator.

sentences.zh: 尋又以蒙遜領張掖太守。

translations.literal: Soon after Mengxun was additionally put in charge as Administrator of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mengxun was also made Zhangye administrator.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，業使蒙遜將萬人攻光弟子純於西郡，經旬不剋，乃引水灌城，窘急乞降，執之以歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Ye sent Mengxun leading ten thousand men to attack Guang's nephew Chun in Xijun; for ten days he did not prevail, then diverted water to flood the city; in distress Chun begged to surrender and was seized and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year Ye sent Mengxun with ten thousand men against Guang's nephew Chun at Xijun; after ten days without success Mengxun flooded the city; Chun surrendered in desperation and was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 時王德叛業，自稱河州刺史，業使蒙遜西討，德焚城，將部曲走投晉昌太守唐瑤，蒙遜追德至沙頭，大破之，虜其妻子部落而還。

translations.literal: At that time Wang De rebelled against Ye and styled himself Inspector of He Province; Ye sent Mengxun west to campaign against him; De burned the city and led his private troops to flee and throw themselves on Jinchang Administrator Tang Yao; Mengxun pursued De to Shatou, utterly defeated him, captured his wife, children, and tribal followers, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De then rebelled, declaring himself He inspector; Ye sent Mengxun west; De burned his city and fled with his followers to Jinchang prefect Tang Yao; Mengxun pursued him to Shatou, routed him, and returned with his family and tribesmen as captives.

sentences.zh: 轉西安太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Administrator of Xi'an; general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xi'an administrator while retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，蒙遜與男成謀殺業，男成不許，蒙遜反譖男成於業，業殺男成。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year Mengxun and Nancheng plotted to kill Ye; Nancheng would not consent; Mengxun in turn slandered Nancheng to Ye, and Ye killed Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year Mengxun plotted with Nancheng to kill Ye; Nancheng refused; Mengxun slandered Nancheng to Ye, and Ye executed Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜乃謂其部曲曰：「段公無道，枉殺輔國。

translations.literal: Mengxun then said to his private troops: "Duke Duan is without the Way and wrongly killed the General Who Assists the State."
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun then told his followers: "Lord Duan is unjust and has wrongly killed the General Who Assists the State."

sentences.zh: 吾為輔國報讎。

translations.literal: I will avenge the General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: I will avenge him.

sentences.zh: 」遂舉兵攻張掖，殺段業，自稱車騎大將軍，[24]建號永安元年。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he raised troops, attacked Zhangye, killed Duan Ye, styled himself Grand General of Agile Cavalry,[24] and established the reign era Yong'an, year one.
translations.idiomatic: " He then marched on Zhangye, killed Duan Ye, declared himself Grand General of Agile Cavalry,[24] and founded the era Yong'an (401).

sentences.zh: 義熙元年正月，李暠改稱大將軍、大都督、涼州牧、護羌校尉、涼公；

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yixi, Li Gao changed his titles to Grand General, Grand Governor, Governor of Liang Province, Protector of the Qiang, and Duke of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yixi (405), Li Gao took the titles Grand General, Grand Governor, Liang governor, Protector of the Qiang, and Duke of Liang;

sentences.zh: 五月，移據酒泉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he moved his base to Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he shifted his seat to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 姚興假傉檀涼州刺史，代王尚屯姑臧。

translations.literal: Yao Xing made Rutan acting Governor of Liang Province; Wang Shang of Dai still encamped at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing appointed Rutan acting Liang governor while Wang Shang of Dai remained garrisoned at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，蒙遜襲李暠，至安彌，去城六十里，暠乃覺。
