translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year Mengxun raided Li Gao, reaching Anmi sixty li from the city before Gao became aware.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year Mengxun struck at Li Gao and reached Anmi, sixty li from the city, before Gao even knew he was coming.

sentences.zh: 引軍出戰，大敗，退還，閉城自守，蒙遜亦歸。

translations.literal: He led the army out to fight, suffered a great defeat, withdrew, shut the city and held it; Mengxun also returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao marched out to give battle, was routed, fell back, and shut himself within the walls; Mengxun withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 六年，蒙遜攻破傉檀，傉檀走屯樂都。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Mengxun defeated Rutan; Rutan fled to encamp at Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Mengxun broke Rutan, who fled to make his stand at Ledu.

sentences.zh: 武威人焦朗入姑臧，自號驃騎大將軍，臣于李暠。

translations.literal: Jiao Lang of Wuwei entered Guzang, styled himself Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and submitted to Li Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Lang of Wuwei seized Guzang, took the title Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and declared himself Li Gao's vassal.

sentences.zh: 八年，蒙遜攻焦朗，殺之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Mengxun attacked Jiao Lang and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Mengxun attacked Jiao Lang and put him to death.

sentences.zh: [25]據姑臧，自號大都督、大將軍、河西王，改稱玄始元年，立子正德為世子。

translations.literal: [25] He seized Guzang, styled himself Grand Governor, Grand General, and King of Hexi, changed the era title to Xuanshi year one, and installed his son Zhengde as heir.
translations.idiomatic: [25] He took Guzang, proclaimed himself Grand Governor, Grand General, and King of Hexi, adopted the reign title Xuanshi (412), and named his son Zhengde heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，李暠死，子歆立。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year Li Gao died; his son Xin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year Li Gao died and was succeeded by his son Xin.

sentences.zh: 六月，歆伐蒙遜，至建康，蒙遜拒之，歆退走，追到西支澗，[26]蒙遜大敗，死者四千餘人，乃收餘眾，增築建康城，置兵戍而還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Xin attacked Mengxun, reaching Jianchang; Mengxun resisted him; Xin retreated; pursued to Xizhi Stream,[26] Mengxun inflicted a great defeat with more than four thousand dead; he then gathered the remaining troops, enlarged and fortified Jianchang city, posted garrison troops, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Xin marched against Mengxun as far as Jianchang; Mengxun held him off and Xin withdrew; pursued to Xizhi Stream,[26] Mengxun won a crushing victory with more than four thousand slain; he then rallied his survivors, strengthened Jianchang's walls, left a garrison, and returned.

sentences.zh: 十四年，蒙遜遣使詣晉，奉表稱蕃，以蒙遜為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Mengxun sent an envoy to Jin, presented a memorial declaring himself a vassal, and was appointed Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Mengxun sent envoys to Jin with a memorial of submission and was confirmed as Liang governor.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，以歆為使持節、都督高昌敦煌晉昌酒泉西海玉門堪泉七郡諸軍事、護羌校尉、征西大將軍、酒泉公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, Xin was made bearer of the staff, Area Commander of the seven commanderies Gaochang, Dunhuang, Jinchang, Jiuquan, Xihai, Yumen, and Kanquan, Protector of the Qiang, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Xin was appointed bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in the seven western commanderies, Protector of the Qiang, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, and Duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 高祖以蒙遜為使持節、散騎常侍、都督涼州諸軍事、鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司、涼州刺史、張掖公。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu made Mengxun bearer of the staff, Regular Attendant at the Palace Writing Office, Area Commander of Liang Province military affairs, Grand General Who Guards the Army, Holder of Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Liang Province, and Duke of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu invested Mengxun as bearer of the staff, palace attendant, Liang area commander, Grand General Who Guards the Army, holder of a Three Excellencies-grade office, Liang governor, and Duke of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 八月，芮芮來抄，蒙遜遣正德距之，正德輕騎進戰，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Rouran came raiding; Mengxun sent Zhengde to resist; Zhengde led light cavalry forward to battle; the army was defeated and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Rouran raided; Mengxun sent Zhengde to meet them; Zhengde charged with light horse, was routed, and killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 乃以次子興國為世子。

translations.literal: He then made his second son Xingguo heir.
translations.idiomatic: He then named his second son Xingguo heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 是歲，進蒙遜侍中、都督涼秦河沙四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、領護匈奴中郎將、西夷校尉、涼州牧，河西王，開府、持節如故。

translations.literal: That year Mengxun was advanced to Palace Attendant, Area Commander of Liang, Qin, He, and Sha four provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Chief Protector of the Xiongnu, Commandant Pacifying the Western Yi, Governor of Liang Province, and King of Hexi; open office and bearing the staff remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mengxun was promoted to palace attendant, commander of the four provinces Liang, Qin, He, and Sha, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, chief protector of the Xiongnu, western commandant, Liang governor, and King of Hexi, retaining his open office and staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉元年，枹罕虜乞佛熾槃出貂渠谷攻河西白草嶺，臨松郡皆沒，執蒙遜從弟成都、從子日蹄、頗羅等而去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, the Qifu barbarian of Fuhan Chipan came out of Diaoqu Valley to attack Baicao Ridge in Hexi; Linsong Commandery was entirely overrun; he seized Mengxun's younger cousin Chengdu, his nephew Riti, Peluo, and others and carried them off.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taizu's first Yuanjia year (424), the Fuhan Qifu Chipan issued from Diaoqu Valley against Baicao Ridge in Hexi, overran all of Linsong Commandery, and carried off Mengxun's cousin Chengdu, his nephews Riti and Peluo, and others.

translations.literal: [28] (Editorial note.)
translations.idiomatic: [28] (Editorial note.)

sentences.zh: 三年，改驃騎為車騎。

translations.literal: In the third year Agile Cavalry was changed to Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his title of Grand General of Agile Cavalry was changed to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世子興國遣使奉表，請周易及子集諸書，太祖並賜之，合四百七十五卷。

translations.literal: Heir Xingguo sent envoys with a memorial requesting the Zhouyi and various collected works; Emperor Taizu bestowed them all, four hundred seventy-five volumes in total.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Xingguo sent a memorial asking for the Book of Changes and other canonical and collected texts; Emperor Taizu granted them all—four hundred seventy-five volumes.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜又就司徒王弘求搜神記，弘寫與之。

translations.literal: Mengxun also asked Minister of Education Wang Hong for the In Search of the Supernatural; Hong copied it out and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun also requested the In Search of the Supernatural from Minister of Education Wang Hong, who copied it out for him.

sentences.zh: 六年，蒙遜征枹罕，時乞佛熾槃死矣，子茂蔓大破蒙遜，生禽興國，殺三千餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Mengxun campaigned against Fuhan; by then Qifu Chipan was already dead; his son Mao Man utterly defeated Mengxun, took Xingguo alive, and killed more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Mengxun marched on Fuhan; Chipan was already dead, and his son Mao Man routed Mengxun, captured Xingguo alive, and slew more than three thousand of his men.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜贖興國，送穀三十萬斛，竟不遣。

translations.literal: Mengxun ransomed Xingguo, sending three hundred thousand hu of grain, but in the end he was not released.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun offered ransom for Xingguo—three hundred thousand hu of grain—but his son was never returned.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜乃立興國母弟菩提為世子，朝廷未知也。

translations.literal: Mengxun then installed Xingguo's younger brother by the same mother, Puti, as heir; the court did not yet know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun then named Xingguo's uterine younger brother Puti heir apparent, of which the court was still unaware.

sentences.zh: 七年，以興國為冠軍將軍、河西王世子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Xingguo was made General Who Establishes Might and heir of the King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the court still recognized Xingguo as General Who Establishes Might and heir of the King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 其年夏四月，西虜赫連定為索虜拓跋燾所破，奔上邽。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month of summer the western barbarian Helian Ding was defeated by the Northern Wei barbarian Tuoba Tao and fled to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, in the fourth month, the western ruler Helian Ding was broken by the Wei emperor Tuoba Tao and fled to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 十一月，茂蔓聞定敗，將家戶及興國東征，欲移居上邽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Mao Man heard that Ding had been defeated; he led his households and Xingguo east on campaign, intending to relocate to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, hearing of Ding's defeat, Mao Man marched east with his clansmen and Xingguo, planning to settle at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 八年正月至南安，定率眾禦茂蔓，大破之，殺茂蔓，執興國而還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he reached Nan'an; Ding led his forces to resist Mao Man, inflicted a great defeat, killed Mao Man, seized Xingguo, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year he reached Nan'an; Ding met Mao Man in force, destroyed him, killed Mao Man, took Xingguo captive, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 四月，定避拓跋燾，欲渡河西擊蒙遜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Ding, avoiding Tuoba Tao, wished to cross west of the river to strike Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, evading Tuoba Tao, Ding planned to cross the river westward and attack Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 五月，率部曲至治城峽口，渡河，濟未半，為吐谷渾慕璝所邀，見獲，興國被創數日死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he led his private troops to Zhicheng Gorge mouth, crossed the river; before the crossing was half complete he was intercepted by Murong Jun of Tuyuhun, captured, and Xingguo, wounded, died after several days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he led his followers to Zhicheng Gorge and entered the river; halfway across he was ambushed by Murong Jun of Tuyuhun and taken; Xingguo, wounded in the fight, died within days.

sentences.zh: 九年，以菩提為冠軍將軍、河西王世子。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Puti was made General Who Establishes Might and heir of the King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Puti was recognized as General Who Establishes Might and heir of the King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，蒙遜卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year Mengxun died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year Mengxun died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 私諡曰武宣王。

translations.literal: His private posthumous title was King Wu-Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the private posthumous title King Wu-Xuan.

sentences.zh: 菩提年幼，蒙遜第三子茂虔時為酒泉太守，[29]眾議推茂虔為主，襲蒙遜位號。

translations.literal: Puti was young; Mengxun's third son Maoqian was then Administrator of Jiuquan;[29] by common counsel Maoqian was pushed forward as lord and succeeded to Mengxun's titles.
translations.idiomatic: Puti was still a child; Mengxun's third son Maoqian was Jiuquan prefect;[29] the leaders acclaimed Maoqian and he inherited Mengxun's rank and titles.

sentences.zh: 十一年，茂虔上表曰：「臣聞功以濟物為高，非竹帛無以述德，名以當實為美，非諡號無以休終。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Maoqian submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that merit is exalted when it aids the world, and without bamboo and silk there is no means to set forth virtue; a name is beautiful when it matches the reality, and without a posthumous title there is no means to bring a life to its proper close."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Maoqian memorialized the throne: "I have learned that true merit lies in benefiting the world, and that virtue cannot be recorded without the written word; that a good name must fit the deed, and that only a posthumous title can properly crown a life's end."

sentences.zh: 先臣蒙遜西復涼城，澤憺崐裔，芟夷羣暴，清灑區夏。

translations.literal: My late lord Mengxun restored the Liang cities in the west, spread his bounty to the Kunlun frontier, cut down the violent multitudes, and cleansed the central realm.
translations.idiomatic: My late father Mengxun recovered the western Liang cities, brought peace to the far Kunlun marches, uprooted the lawless hosts, and cleared the heartland of turmoil.

sentences.zh: 暨運鍾有道，備大宋之宗臣，爵班九服，享惟永之丕祚，功名昭著，剋固貞節。

translations.literal: When fortune turned to the Way, he stood among the Great Song's vassal lords, his rank placed among the nine domains, enjoying enduring great blessing; his achievements and fame were manifest, and he firmly upheld loyal constancy.
translations.idiomatic: When a righteous age dawned he became a vassal prince of Great Song, ranked among the nine domains, blessed with enduring fortune; his fame was bright and his loyalty unshaken.

sentences.zh: 考終由正，而請名之路無階，懿跡雖弘，而述敍之美有缺。

translations.literal: He met his end in the proper way, yet the path to request a name had no steps; though his excellent traces were broad, the beauty of their narration had a gap.
translations.idiomatic: He died as he had lived, yet there was no avenue by which to petition a posthumous name; though his noble deeds were great, their full commemoration remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 臣子痛感，咸用不安。

translations.literal: Your servant and his sons are pained at heart and all feel unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and I are stricken with grief and cannot rest easy.

sentences.zh: 謹案諡法，剋定禍亂曰武，善聞周達曰宣。

translations.literal: Respectfully consulting the posthumous-name canon: overcoming and settling calamity and disorder is called Wu; good renown reaching far and wide is called Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: According to the canon of posthumous titles, to overcome chaos is Wu, and to be known for wisdom reaching all quarters is Xuan.

sentences.zh: 先臣廓清河外，勳光天府，標牓稱迹，實兼斯義。

translations.literal: My late lord broadened the lands beyond the Yellow River; his merit shone upon the celestial storehouse; his proclaimed deeds and titles truly embrace both these meanings.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the country beyond the Yellow River; his merit lit the court; the record of his deeds truly fulfills both meanings.

sentences.zh: 輒上諡為武宣王。

translations.literal: I therefore submit the posthumous title King Wu-Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore propose the posthumous title King Wu-Xuan.

sentences.zh: 若允天聽，垂之史筆，則幽顯荷榮，始終無恨。

translations.literal: If Heaven's ear approves and it is handed down to the historian's brush, then the hidden and the manifest alike will bear honor, and from beginning to end there will be no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty grants this and it is inscribed by the historians, the living and the dead alike will share in glory, and his course will be complete without regret.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「使持節、侍中、都督秦河沙涼四州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、領護匈奴中郎將、西夷校尉、涼州牧河西王蒙遜，才兼文武，勳濟西服，爰自萬里，款誠夙著，方仗忠果，翼宣遠略，奄至薨隕，悽悼于懷。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Bearer of the staff, Palace Attendant, Area Commander of Qin, He, Sha, and Liang four provinces, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Holder of Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, Chief Protector of the Xiongnu, Commandant Pacifying the Western Yi, Governor of Liang Province, King of Hexi Mengxun—talent embracing both civil and military, merit aiding the western lands, from ten thousand li away his sincere allegiance was long manifest; we were just relying on his loyal resolve to assist our far-reaching design, when suddenly he passed away, and grief fills our breast."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "Mengxun, King of Hexi—bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander of Qin, He, Sha, and Liang, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, holder of a Three Excellencies-grade office, chief protector of the Xiongnu, western commandant, and Liang governor—combined civil and military gifts and served the western realm; though he dwelt ten thousand li away, his loyalty was long proven. We had counted on his steadfast heart to advance our distant strategy, and his sudden death fills us with sorrow."

sentences.zh: 便遣使弔祭，并加顯諡。

translations.literal: Let envoys be sent at once to offer condolences and sacrifices, and let an eminent posthumous title also be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys shall be sent to mourn and sacrifice on our behalf, and an official posthumous title shall be conferred.

sentences.zh: 嗣子茂虔，纂戎前軌，乃心彌彰，宜蒙寵授，紹茲蕃業。

translations.literal: His successor Maoqian inherits the former path of arms; his loyal heart shines all the more; he should receive favor and appointment to continue this frontier enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Maoqian follows his father's martial course with redoubled loyalty and deserves imperial favor to carry on this border kingdom.

sentences.zh: 可持節、散騎常侍、都督涼秦河沙四州諸軍事、征西大將軍、領護匈奴中郎將、西夷校尉、涼州刺史、河西王。」

translations.literal: He may bear the staff, serve as Regular Attendant at the Palace Writing Office, be Area Commander of Liang, Qin, He, and Sha four provinces, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Chief Protector of the Xiongnu, Commandant Pacifying the Western Yi, Inspector of Liang Province, and King of Hexi."
translations.idiomatic: Let him bear the staff, serve as palace attendant, command the four provinces Liang, Qin, He, and Sha, hold the title Grand General Who Pacifies the West, serve as chief protector of the Xiongnu and western commandant, govern Liang Province, and reign as King of Hexi."

sentences.zh: 河西人趙𢾺善歷算。

translations.literal: Zhao Fu of Hexi was skilled in calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Hexi named Zhao Fu was expert in astronomy and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 十四年，茂虔奉表獻方物，并獻周生子十三卷，時務論十二卷，三國總略二十卷，俗問十一卷，十三州志十卷，文檢六卷，四科傳四卷，燉煌實錄十卷，涼書十卷，漢皇德傳二十五卷，亡典七卷，魏駮九卷，謝艾集八卷，古今字二卷，乘丘先生三卷，[30]周髀一卷，皇帝王歷三合紀一卷，趙𢾺傳并甲寅元歷一卷，孔子讚一卷，合一百五十四卷。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Maoqian submitted a memorial presenting tribute goods and also presented Zhou's Birth in thirteen scrolls, Discourse on Current Affairs in twelve scrolls, Comprehensive Summary of the Three Kingdoms in twenty scrolls, Popular Questions in eleven scrolls, Gazetteer of the Thirteen Provinces in ten scrolls, Literary Examination in six scrolls, Biographies of the Four Categories in four scrolls, Veritable Records of Dunhuang in ten scrolls, Book of Liang in ten scrolls, Chronicle of Han Imperial Virtue in twenty-five scrolls, Lost Canons in seven scrolls, Wei Refutations in nine scrolls, Collected Works of Xie Ai in eight scrolls, Ancient and Modern Characters in two scrolls, Master of Chengqiu in three scrolls,[30] Zhou Bi in one scroll, Chronicle of the Three Unions of Imperial Kings in one scroll, Biography of Zhao Fu together with the Jiayin Origin Calendar in one scroll, and Eulogy of Confucius in one scroll—a total of one hundred fifty-four scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Maoqian sent tribute and presented one hundred fifty-four scrolls of books, including the Zhou's Birth, Discourse on Current Affairs, Comprehensive Summary of the Three Kingdoms, Popular Questions, Gazetteer of the Thirteen Provinces, Literary Examination, Biographies of the Four Categories, Veritable Records of Dunhuang, Book of Liang, Chronicle of Han Imperial Virtue, Lost Canons, Wei Refutations, Collected Works of Xie Ai, Ancient and Modern Characters, Master of Chengqiu,[30] Zhou Bi, Chronicle of the Three Unions of Imperial Kings, the Biography of Zhao Fu with the Jiayin Origin Calendar, and Eulogy of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 茂虔又求晉、趙起居注諸雜書數十件，太祖賜之。

translations.literal: Maoqian also requested several dozen miscellaneous works such as the Jin and Zhao Court Diaries; Emperor Taizu bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqian also asked for several dozen court records and miscellanies from Jin and Zhao times, and Emperor Taizu granted them.

sentences.zh: 十六年閏八月，拓跋燾攻涼州，茂虔兄子萬年為虜內應，茂虔見執。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month of the sixteenth year Tuoba Tao attacked Liang Province; Maoqian's elder brother's son Wannian acted as the enemy's inside agent within, and Maoqian was seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month of the sixteenth year Tuoba Tao invaded Liang Province; Maoqian's nephew Wannian betrayed him from within, and Maoqian was captured.

sentences.zh: 茂虔弟安彌縣侯無諱先為征西將軍、沙州刺史、都督建康以西諸軍事、酒泉太守，第六弟武興縣侯儀德為征東將軍、秦州刺史、都督丹嶺以西諸軍事、張掖太守。

translations.literal: Maoqian's younger brother, Marquis of Anmi Wuju, had earlier been Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Sha Province, Area Commander of military affairs west of Jianchang, and Administrator of Jiuquan; the sixth younger brother, Marquis of Wuxing Yide, was Grand General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Qin Province, Area Commander of military affairs west of Danling, and Administrator of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqian's brother Wuju, Marquis of Anmi, had been Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Sha inspector, commander west of Jianchang, and Jiuquan prefect; his sixth brother Yide, Marquis of Wuxing, was Grand General Who Pacifies the East, Qin inspector, commander west of Danling, and Zhangye prefect.

sentences.zh: [31]燾既獲茂虔，遣軍擊儀德，棄城奔無諱。

translations.literal: [31] After Tao had captured Maoqian, he sent troops to strike Yide; Yide abandoned the city and fled to Wuju.
translations.idiomatic: [31] Once Tao held Maoqian prisoner, he sent forces against Yide, who abandoned his city and fled to Wuju.

sentences.zh: 於是無諱、儀德擁家戶西就從弟敦煌太守唐兒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wuju and Yide led their households west to join their younger cousin by the father's line, Dunhuang Administrator Tang Er.
translations.idiomatic: Wuju and Yide then moved west with their clansmen to join their cousin Tang Er, prefect of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 燾使將守武威、酒泉、張掖而還。

translations.literal: Tao left generals to guard Wuwei, Jiuquan, and Zhangye and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tao left garrisons at Wuwei, Jiuquan, and Zhangye and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，無諱使唐兒守敦煌，自與儀德伐酒泉，三月，剋之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year Wuju made Tang Er guard Dunhuang and himself with Yide attacked Jiuquan; in the third month they took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year Wuju left Tang Er to hold Dunhuang and marched with Yide on Jiuquan, which fell in the third month.

sentences.zh: 攻張掖、臨松，得四萬餘戶，還據酒泉。

translations.literal: They attacked Zhangye and Linsong, gained more than forty thousand households, and returned to hold Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Zhangye and Linsong, seized more than forty thousand households, and withdrew to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 十八年五月，唐兒反，無諱留從弟天周守酒泉，復與儀德討唐兒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year Tang Er rebelled; Wuju left his younger cousin Tianzhou to guard Jiuquan and again with Yide campaigned against Tang Er.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year Tang Er revolted; Wuju left his cousin Tianzhou at Jiuquan and marched again with Yide to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 唐兒將萬餘人出戰，大敗，執唐兒殺之，復據敦煌。

translations.literal: Tang Er led more than ten thousand men out to fight, suffered a great defeat, was seized and killed, and they again held Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Er marched out with ten thousand men, was routed, captured, and executed; Wuju then reoccupied Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 七月，拓跋燾遣軍圍酒泉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Tuoba Tao sent troops to besiege Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Tuoba Tao laid siege to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 十月，城中饑，萬餘口皆餓死，天周殺妻以食戰士，食盡，城乃陷，執天周至平城，殺之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month famine struck within the city; more than ten thousand people starved to death; Tianzhou killed his wife to feed the warriors; when food was exhausted the city fell; Tianzhou was seized, taken to Pingcheng, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth month starvation had killed more than ten thousand in the city; Tianzhou slew his wife to feed his soldiers; when provisions ran out the city fell; he was taken to Pingcheng and executed.

sentences.zh: 于時虜兵甚盛，無諱眾饑，懼不自立，欲引眾西行。

translations.literal: At that time the enemy forces were very strong; Wuju's followers were hungry; fearing he could not stand, he wished to lead the multitude westward.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei armies were overwhelming; Wuju's men were starving; fearing he could not hold out, he planned to lead his people west.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣弟安周五千人伐鄯善，堅守不下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he sent his younger brother Anzhou with five thousand men to attack Shanshan; they held firm and he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent his brother Anzhou with five thousand men against Shanshan, but the city held and would not fall.

sentences.zh: 十九年四月，無諱自率萬餘家棄敦煌，西就安周，未至而鄯善王比龍將四千餘家走，因據鄯善。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year Wuju himself led more than ten thousand households, abandoned Dunhuang, and went west to join Anzhou; before he arrived, the King of Shanshan Bilong led more than four thousand households away, and thereby seized Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year Wuju abandoned Dunhuang at the head of ten thousand-odd households to join Anzhou in the west; before he arrived, King Bilong of Shanshan fled with four thousand households and seized the kingdom for himself.

sentences.zh: 初，唐契自晉昌奔伊吾，是年攻高昌，高昌城主闞爽告急。

translations.literal: Earlier Tang Qi had fled from Jinchang to Yiwu; that year he attacked Gaochang; the lord of Gaochang city Kan Shuang sent urgent word for help.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tang Qi had fled Jinchang for Yiwu; that year he attacked Gaochang, and the city's ruler Kan Shuang sent an urgent appeal for aid.

sentences.zh: [32]八月，無諱留從子豐周守鄯善，自將家戶赴之。

translations.literal: [32] In the eighth month Wuju left his nephew Fengzhou to guard Shanshan and himself led his households to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: [32] In the eighth month Wuju left his nephew Fengzhou at Shanshan and marched in person with his clansmen to relieve Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 未至，而芮芮遣軍救高昌，殺唐契，部曲奔無諱。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Rouran sent troops to rescue Gaochang, killed Tang Qi, and his private troops fled to Wuju.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, the Rouran sent an army to save Gaochang, killed Tang Qi, and his followers fled to Wuju.

sentences.zh: 九月，無諱遣將衞尞夜襲高昌，[33]爽奔芮芮，無諱復據高昌。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wuju sent the general Wei Liao to raid Gaochang by night;[33] Shuang fled to Rouran, and Wuju again held Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wuju sent Wei Liao to storm Gaochang by night;[33] Shuang fled to the Rouran, and Wuju reoccupied the city.

sentences.zh: 遣常侍氾儁奉表使京師，獻方物。

translations.literal: He sent Regular Attendant Fan Jun with a memorial as envoy to the capital, presenting tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Regular Attendant Fan Jun to the capital with a memorial and tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔曰：「往年狡虜縱逸，侵害涼土，西河王茂虔遂至不守，淪陷寇逆，累世著誠，以為矜悼。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu issued an edict saying: "In former years the cunning barbarians ran wild and encroached upon the Liang lands; the King of Hexi Maoqian came even to the point of not holding his ground and fell to the invaders; yet his house's loyalty over many generations moves us to compassionate grief."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu decreed: "In years past the northern invaders ravaged the western lands; King Maoqian of Hexi could not hold his realm and was overrun; yet his family's loyalty through generations stirs our pity."

sentences.zh: 次弟無諱克紹遺業，保據方隅，外結鄰國，內輯民庶，係心闕庭，踐修貢職，宜加朝命，以褒篤勳。

translations.literal: The next younger brother Wuju has been able to continue the legacy, guard and hold a corner of the realm, bind himself to neighboring states abroad and put the people in order within, keep his heart tied to the imperial court, and practice tribute duties; he should receive court appointment to reward his steadfast merit."
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wuju has inherited the cause, held a distant corner of the empire, secured foreign allies and governed his people, kept faith with the throne, and fulfilled tribute obligations; he deserves imperial appointment in reward for his steadfast service."

sentences.zh: 可持節、散騎常侍、都督涼河沙三州諸軍事、征西大將軍、領護匈奴中郎將、西夷校尉、涼州刺史、河西王。」

translations.literal: He may bear the staff, serve as Regular Attendant at the Palace Writing Office, be Area Commander of Liang, He, and Sha three provinces, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Chief Protector of the Xiongnu, Commandant Pacifying the Western Yi, Inspector of Liang Province, and King of Hexi."
translations.idiomatic: Let him bear the staff, serve as palace attendant, command Liang, He, and Sha, hold the title Grand General Who Pacifies the West, serve as chief protector of the Xiongnu and western commandant, govern Liang Province, and reign as King of Hexi."

sentences.zh: 無諱卒，弟安周立。

translations.literal: Wuju died; his younger brother Anzhou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wuju died and was succeeded by his brother Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，詔曰：「故征西大將軍、河西王無諱弟安周，才略沈到，世篤忠欵，統承遺業，民眾歸懷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year an edict said: "The younger brother of the late Grand General Who Pacifies the West, King of Hexi Wuju—Anzhou—has deep talent and penetrating strategy, generations of steadfast loyalty, inherits and carries on the legacy, and the people turn to him with trust."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the court decreed: "Anzhou, brother of the late King Wuju of Hexi, is gifted and resolute, his house loyal through generations; he has taken up his brother's legacy and won the people's hearts."

sentences.zh: 雖亡士喪師，孤立異所，而能招率殘寡，攘寇自今，宜加榮授，垂軌先烈。

translations.literal: Though he has lost soldiers and suffered defeat, stands alone in a strange land, yet he can rally the scattered remnants, drive off the enemy from this day forward, and should receive honored appointment to hand down the track of his forebears."
translations.idiomatic: Though he has lost men and stands isolated in a foreign land, he has rallied the survivors and beaten back the invaders; he deserves high honor that may stand beside his forefathers' fame."

sentences.zh: 可使持節、散騎常侍、都督涼河沙三州諸軍事、領西域戊己校尉、涼州刺史、河西王。

translations.literal: He may bear the staff, serve as Regular Attendant at the Palace Writing Office, be Area Commander of Liang, He, and Sha three provinces, hold the post of Commandant of the Wuji Garrison in the Western Regions, be Inspector of Liang Province, and King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Let him bear the staff, serve as palace attendant, command Liang, He, and Sha, hold the western garrison command, govern Liang Province, and reign as King of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 」世祖大明三年，安周奉獻方物。

translations.literal: " In the third year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, Anzhou presented tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: " In Emperor Shizu's third Daming year (459), Anzhou sent tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：氐藉世業之資，胡因倔起之眾，結根百頃，跨有河西，雖戎夷猾夏，自擅荒服，而財力雄富，頗尚禮文。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Di relied on the resources of hereditary enterprise; the Hu arose through the strength of a defiant uprising; rooted at Baigeng, they spanned Hexi; though as barbarians of the frontier they troubled the central lands and held the wild marches for themselves, their wealth and power were mighty and they greatly esteemed ritual and letters.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Di drew on generations of accumulated strength; the Hu rose from a defiant tribal host; rooted at Baigeng, they held Hexi; though frontier peoples who troubled the heartland and ruled the outer wastes, they grew rich and powerful and cultivated ritual and learning.

sentences.zh: 楊氏兵精地險，境接華漢，伺隙邊關，首鼠疆埸，遂西入白馬，東出黃金，乘晉壽之捷，構圍涪之釁，規吞黑水，志傾井絡，紀、郢之勢方危，樊、鄧之心屢駭。

translations.literal: The Yang clan had crack troops and perilous terrain; their territory bordered the Chinese heartland; they watched for gaps along the border passes and wavered at the frontier marches; they then entered Baima in the west and issued from Huangjin in the east; riding the victory at Jinshou, they contrived the provocation of besieging Fu; they plotted to swallow the Black River and aimed to overturn the Well-Cable region; the positions of Ji and Ying were just then endangered, and the hearts of Fan and Deng were repeatedly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang were fierce soldiers on treacherous ground, their lands touching the Chinese heartland; they probed the border passes and hedged along the frontier, thrust west into Baima and east from Huangjin, exploited the victory at Jinshou to provoke the siege of Fu, aimed to seize the Black River and overturn Shu, threatened Ji and Ying, and repeatedly terrified Fan and Deng.

sentences.zh: 天子聽朝不怡，有懷辛、李之將，而齊之宣皇，率偏旅數百，定命先驅，推鋒直指，勢踰風電，雲徹席卷，致屆南城，逐北追奔，全勝萬里，敵人皆裹骨輿屍，越至險而自竄，其餘皆膏身山野，委骸川澤。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven heard court with displeasure and cherished generals like Xin and Li; but Qi's Illustrious Emperor led a few hundred of a detached column as the vanguard who fixed destiny, pushed the spearhead straight forward with momentum surpassing wind and lightning, clouds dispersing and rolling up in a sweep, arriving at Nan commandery city, pursuing the fleeing north in chase, winning completely for ten thousand li; the enemy all wrapped bones and bore corpses, crossed the utmost peril and fled of themselves; the rest all greased the mountains and wilds with their bodies and cast their bones in rivers and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sat troubled at court, longing for generals like Xin and Li; then Qi's Illustrious Emperor led a few hundred men as destiny's vanguard, drove straight forward swifter than storm and lightning, swept the field like rolling clouds, reached Nan commandery, pursued the fleeing foe for ten thousand li to total victory; the enemy wrapped their dead and fled the steepest passes; the rest littered the mountains and rivers with their corpses.

sentences.zh: 既而裴、劉二將，藉其威聲，故使濁水靡旗，蘭臯失嶮，氐族轉徙奔亡，遺燼不滅者若綖，梁土獲乂，以迄于今。

translations.literal: Thereafter the two generals Pei and Liu, borrowing that martial renown, thereby made the muddy waters lower their banners and Langao lose its defiles; the Di clans turned and migrated in flight; embers not yet extinguished were like threads; the Liang lands obtained order, down to the present day.
translations.idiomatic: Then Generals Pei and Liu, riding that renown, broke the enemy at Zhuoshui and Langao; the Di were driven into exile, their last embers scattered like threads; the Liang realm was pacified, and peace has held to this day.

sentences.zh: 由此而言，功烈可謂盛矣。

translations.literal: Judging from this, their achievements and splendor may be called great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: By this measure, their achievements were truly magnificent.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 晉武假征西將軍 「征西將軍」魏書氐傳、通典邊防典作「平西將軍」。

translations.literal: Jin Wu appointed acting Grand General Who Pacifies the West — "Grand General Who Pacifies the West" in the Wei Shu Di biography and the Tongdian Frontier Administration reads "Grand General Who Levels the West."
translations.idiomatic: On Jin Wu's appointment of an acting Grand General Who Pacifies the West: the Wei Shu Di biography and Tongdian Frontier Administration read Grand General Who Levels the West (Pingxi) instead.

sentences.zh: 名戊搜 「戊搜」，魏書氐傳、通典邊防典作「茂搜」。

translations.literal: Named Wusou — "Wusou" in the Wei Shu Di biography and the Tongdian Frontier Administration reads "Maosou."
translations.idiomatic: The name Wusou: the Wei Shu Di biography and Tongdian Frontier Administration have Maosou instead.

sentences.zh: 與堅頭分部曲 據魏書氐傳，堅頭，難敵弟。

translations.literal: Divided the private troops with Jiantou — according to the Wei Shu Di biography, Jiantou was Nandi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: On dividing the troops with Jiantou: according to the Wei Shu Di biography, Jiantou was Nandi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 初子國率左右誅式王及宋奴 各本並脫「初」字，據魏書氐傳補。

translations.literal: At first Zi Guo led his attendants to execute the Prince of Shi and Songnu — all editions omit the character "at first," supplied according to the Wei Shu Di biography.
translations.idiomatic: On Zi Guo leading his men to kill the Prince of Shi and Songnu: all editions drop the word "first," restored from the Wei Shu Di biography.

sentences.zh: 自號隴西王 各本並脫「隴」字，據魏書氐傳、晉書前秦載記補。

translations.literal: Styled himself King of Longxi — all editions omit the character "Long," supplied according to the Wei Shu Di biography and the Jin Shu Former Qin annals.
translations.idiomatic: On his styling himself King of Longxi: all editions omit Long, restored from the Wei Shu Di biography and Jin Shu Former Qin annals.

sentences.zh: 興遣將王敏攻城因梁州別駕呂瑩求救於盛盛遣軍次濜口敏退 據晉書姚興載記：「晉義熙二年，平北將軍、梁州督護苻宣入漢中，興梁州別駕呂瑩、漢中徐逸、席難起兵應宣，求救於楊盛。

translations.literal: Xing sent the general Wang Min to attack the city; because Liang Province Attendant-in-Office Lü Ying sought rescue from Sheng, Sheng sent troops to encamp at Jin Ford and Min withdrew — according to the Jin Shu annals of Yao Xing: "In the second year of Yixi of Jin, the General Who Pacifies the North, Liang Area Protector Fu Xuan entered Hanzhong; Xing's Liang Attendant Lü Ying, Hanzhong's Xu Yi, and Xi Nan raised troops in response to Xuan and sought rescue from Yang Sheng."
translations.idiomatic: On Yao Xing sending Wang Min to attack the city and Yang Sheng relieving Lü Ying at Jin Ford: the Jin Shu annals of Yao Xing read, "In Jin's second Yixi year (406), Fu Xuan, area protector of Liang, entered Hanzhong; Lü Ying, Xu Yi, and Xi Nan rose in support and appealed to Yang Sheng."

sentences.zh: 盛遣軍臨濜口，南梁州刺史王敏退守武興。

translations.literal: Sheng sent troops to approach Jin Ford; the Southern Liang Inspector Wang Min withdrew to guard Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng marched to Jin Ford; Southern Liang inspector Wang Min fell back to Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 」通鑑晉安帝義熙三年：「氐王楊盛以平北將軍苻宣為梁州督護，將兵入漢中，秦梁州別駕呂瑩等起兵應之。

translations.literal: " The Zizhi Tongjian for the third year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin: "The Di king Yang Sheng made the General Who Pacifies the North Fu Xuan area protector of Liang, led troops into Hanzhong, and Qin Liang Attendant Lü Ying and others raised troops in response."
translations.idiomatic: " The Comprehensive Mirror, Jin Emperor An's third Yixi year (407): "The Di king Yang Sheng installed Fu Xuan as Liang area protector and entered Hanzhong; Lü Ying and others of Liang rose to join him."

sentences.zh: 刺史王敏攻之，瑩等求援於盛。

translations.literal: Inspector Wang Min attacked them; Ying and the others sought rescue from Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Wang Min attacked them; Ying and his allies appealed to Yang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 盛遣軍臨濜口，敏退屯武興。

translations.literal: Sheng sent troops to approach Jin Ford; Min withdrew and encamped at Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng advanced to Jin Ford; Min withdrew to Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 」可證宋書氐傳此段文有脫譌。

translations.literal: " This proves that this passage in the Song Shu Di biography has omissions and errors.
translations.idiomatic: " This confirms that the Song Shu Di biography passage is corrupt and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 宣乃還 北監本、毛本作「宣」，三朝本、殿本、局本作「寧」。

translations.literal: Xuan then returned — the Northern Supervisor edition and Mao edition read "Xuan"; the Three-Reigns, Hall, and Bureau editions read "Ning."
translations.idiomatic: On "Xuan then returned": the Northern Supervisor and Mao editions read Xuan; the Three-Reigns, Hall, and Bureau editions read Ning.

sentences.zh: 按上文作「苻宣」，晉書姚興載記、通鑑亦作「苻宣」。

translations.literal: According to the text above it is written "Fu Xuan"; the Jin Shu annals of Yao Xing and the Zizhi Tongjian also write "Fu Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: The passage above has Fu Xuan, as do the Jin Shu annals of Yao Xing and the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 作「宣」是，今訂正。

translations.literal: Writing "Xuan" is correct; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan is correct; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 太祖即以玄為使持節征西將軍平羌校尉北秦州刺史武都王 「太祖」各本並作「明帝」。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu then made Xuan bearer of the staff, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Commandant Pacifying the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin Province, and King of Wudu — "Emperor Taizu" in all editions reads "Emperor Ming."
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Taizu's appointment of Xuan as bearer of the staff, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Qiang commandant, Northern Qin inspector, and King of Wudu: all editions read Emperor Ming instead of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 龔道耕蛛隱廬日箋云：「此段並述元嘉中事，明帝當作太祖。

translations.literal: Gong Daogeng's Zhuyinlu commentary says: "This passage altogether relates events of the Yuanjia era; Emperor Ming should read Emperor Taizu."
translations.idiomatic: Gong Daogeng's Zhuyinlu commentary notes: "This whole passage describes Yuanjia-era events; Emperor Ming should be Emperor Taizu."

sentences.zh: 」按龔說是，今改正。

translations.literal: " According to Gong's view this is correct; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: " Gong's reading is accepted; the text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 法護將下 「將」字下各本並衍「軍」字，據通鑑宋元嘉十年刪。

translations.literal: Below Fa Hu jiang — below the character "jiang" all editions redundantly add "jun," deleted according to the Zizhi Tongjian for the tenth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: On the passage "Fa Hu jiang": below "jiang" every edition spuriously adds "jun," removed per the Comprehensive Mirror, Yuanjia year 10.

sentences.zh: 難當釋保宗遣鎮童亭 「童亭」魏書氐傳、通鑑作「董亭」。

translations.literal: Nan Dang released Bao Zong and sent him to garrison Tongting — "Tongting" in the Wei Shu Di biography and the Zizhi Tongjian reads "Dongting."
translations.idiomatic: On Nan Dang releasing Bao Zong to hold Tongting: the Wei Shu Di biography and Comprehensive Mirror read Dongting instead of Tongting.

sentences.zh: 水經渭水注：「涇谷水又東北歷董亭下。

translations.literal: Commentary on the Wei River in the Shuijing: "The Jing Valley stream again flowed northeast past Dongting below."
translations.idiomatic: The Shuijing commentary on the Wei River reads: "The Jing Valley waters again ran northeast below Dongting."

sentences.zh: 楊難當使兄子保宗鎮董亭，即此亭也。」

translations.literal: Yang Nan Dang sent his elder brother's son Bao Zong to garrison Dongting — this is that pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nan Dang stationed his nephew Bao Zong at Dongting — the very place named here."

sentences.zh: 保宗奔 「奔」字下疑脫「索虜」二字。

translations.literal: Bao Zong fled — below the character "fled" the two characters "Suolu" are suspected to be missing.
translations.idiomatic: On "Bao Zong fled": the words "the Northern Wei" are probably lost after "fled."

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史劉真道擊斬沖 「劉真道」各本並作「劉道真」，據本書劉懷肅傳真道附傳乙正。

translations.literal: Liang Inspector Liu Zhendao struck and beheaded Chong — "Liu Zhendao" in all editions reads "Liu Daozhen," corrected according to the appended biography of Zhendao in the Liu Huaisu zhuan of this book.
translations.idiomatic: On Liang inspector Liu Zhendao slaying Chong: all editions read Liu Daozhen; restored from the Zhendao appendix in this book's Liu Huaisu biography.

sentences.zh: 下出並改。

translations.literal: Occurrences below are likewise changed.
translations.idiomatic: All following instances are emended the same way.

sentences.zh: 巴西太守劉道錫嬰城固守 「劉道錫」各本並作「劉道銀」，據建康實錄、通鑑宋元嘉十八年改。

translations.literal: Baxi Administrator Liu Daoxi closed the city and held firm — "Liu Daoxi" in all editions reads "Liu Daoyin," changed according to the Jiankang Shilu and the Zizhi Tongjian for the eighteenth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: On Baxi administrator Liu Daoxi defending the walled city: every edition reads Liu Daoyin; emended per the Jiankang Veritable Records and Comprehensive Mirror, Yuanjia year 18.

sentences.zh: 按劉道錫見本書卷六五劉道產傳。

translations.literal: Liu Daoxi appears in juan 65, the Liu Daochan zhuan of this book.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoxi is attested in juan 65 of this work, the biography of Liu Daochan.

sentences.zh: 安西參軍魯尚期追難當出寒峽 「寒峽」水經漾水注作「塞峽」。

translations.literal: Anxi Staff Officer Lu Shangqi pursued Nan Dang out of Han Gorge — "Han Gorge" in the Shuijing commentary on the Yang River reads "Sai Gorge."
translations.idiomatic: On Anxi staff officer Lu Shangqi driving Nan Dang from Han Gorge: the Shuijing's Yang River commentary reads Sai Gorge.

sentences.zh: 達追擊斬齊 通鑑考異云：「後魏河間公齊傳云：『文德求援於宋，宋遣房亮之、苻昭、啖龍等帥眾助文德，斬龍，禽亮之，氐遂平，以功拜內都大官，卒。

translations.literal: Da pursued, struck, and beheaded Qi — the Zizhi Tongjian Kaoyi says: "The Later Wei biography of Duke of Hejian Qi says: 'Wende sought rescue from Song; Song sent Fang Liangzhi, Fu Zhao, Dan Long, and others to lead troops to aid Wende; Long was beheaded, Liangzhi captured, the Di were then pacified; for merit he was appointed Inner Metropolitan Grand Officer and died.'"
translations.idiomatic: On Da pursuing and killing Qi: the Comprehensive Mirror's collation notes cite the Later Wei Hejian Duke Qi biography — Wende called on Song; Song sent Fang Liangzhi, Fu Zhao, and Dan Long; Long was killed, Liangzhi taken, the Di subdued, and Qi rose to Inner Metropolitan Grand Officer before his death.

sentences.zh: 』然則宋書誤也。」

translations.literal: " Thus the Song Shu is in error."
translations.idiomatic: " The Song Shu account is therefore mistaken."

sentences.zh: 楊氏世祖西勞方忠累葉 張森楷校勘記云：「疑當作『楊氏世祖西方，勞忠累葉。』」

translations.literal: Yang clan ancestral lord west labored loyal through many generations — Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "Suspected to read 'Yang clan ancestral lord of the west, labored in loyalty through many generations.'"
translations.idiomatic: On "the Yang ancestral lord west labored in loyalty for generations": Zhang Senkai's note proposes punctuating it as "the Yang ancestral lord of the west, who toiled in loyalty through many generations."

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史王玄謨上表曰 各本並脫「玄」字，據通鑑宋孝武帝孝建二年補。

translations.literal: Yong Inspector Wang Xuanmo submitted a memorial — all editions omit the character "Xuan," supplied according to the Zizhi Tongjian for the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: On Yong inspector Wang Xuanmo's memorial: every edition drops Xuan, restored from the Comprehensive Mirror, Emperor Xiaowu's second Xiaojian year.

sentences.zh: 文度遣弟龍驤將軍文弘伐仇池 「文弘」魏書本紀作「楊黽」，氐傳作「楊鼠」。

translations.literal: Wendu sent his younger brother, Dragon-soaring General Wen Hong, to attack Chouchi — "Wen Hong" in the Wei Shu basic annals reads "Yang Min," and the Di biography reads "Yang Shu."
translations.idiomatic: On Wendu dispatching his brother, Dragon-soaring General Wen Hong, against Chouchi: the Wei Shu annals read Yang Min, the Di biography Yang Shu.

sentences.zh: 蓋魏獻文帝名弘，魏史臣避諱改之。

translations.literal: This is because Northern Wei Emperor Xianwen was named Hong; Wei historians altered it to avoid the taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei historians changed the name to avoid the taboo on Emperor Xianwen, whose personal name was Hong.

sentences.zh: 封狄地王 晉書載記作「北地王」。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as King of Di — the Jin Shu annals read "King of the North."
translations.idiomatic: On his enfeoffment as King of Di: the Jin Shu annals call him King of the North.

sentences.zh: 又以蒙遜叔父羅仇為西平太守 「叔父」晉書載記作「伯父」。

translations.literal: Again made Mengxun's uncle Luo Chou Western Ping Administrator — "uncle (father's younger brother)" in the Jin Shu annals reads "uncle (father's elder brother)."
translations.idiomatic: On Mengxun's appointing his uncle Luo Chou to Western Ping: the Jin Shu annals read "father's elder brother" rather than "father's younger brother."

sentences.zh: 殺酒泉太守疊滕 「疊滕」晉書載記、通鑑作「壘澄」。

translations.literal: Killed Jiuquan Administrator Die Teng — "Die Teng" in the Jin Shu annals and the Zizhi Tongjian reads "Lei Cheng."
translations.idiomatic: On the killing of Jiuquan administrator Die Teng: the Jin Shu annals and Comprehensive Mirror read Lei Cheng.

sentences.zh: 業以蒙遜為鎮西將軍臨池太守 「臨池太守」晉書載記、通鑑晉安帝隆安二年作「臨池侯」。

translations.literal: Ye made Mengxun Grand General Who Guards the West and Linchi Administrator — "Linchi Administrator" in the Jin Shu annals and the Zizhi Tongjian for the second year of Longan under Emperor An of Jin reads "Marquis of Linchi."
translations.idiomatic: On Ye appointing Mengxun Grand General Who Guards the West and Linchi administrator: the Jin Shu annals and Comprehensive Mirror (Jin Emperor An, Longan year 2) read Marquis of Linchi.

sentences.zh: 自稱車騎大將軍 御覽一二四引十六國春秋北涼錄作「大將軍、涼州牧」。

translations.literal: Styled himself Grand Cavalry General — Imperial Readings 124, citing the Northern Liang Records of the Spring and Autumn of the Sixteen Kingdoms, reads "Grand General, Governor of Liang."
translations.idiomatic: On his styling himself Grand Cavalry General: Imperial Readings 124, citing the Northern Liang Records, gives only Grand General and Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 晉書載記作「使持節、大都督、大將軍、涼州牧、張掖公」。

translations.literal: The Jin Shu annals read "Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander, Grand General, Governor of Liang, Duke of Zhangye."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Shu annals list him as bearer of the staff, grand commander, grand general, governor of Liang, and duke of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 並無「車騎大將軍」之稱。

translations.literal: Neither has the title "Grand Cavalry General."
translations.idiomatic: Neither source gives him the title Grand Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜攻焦朗殺之 錢大昕廿二史考異云：「晉書云攻朗，克而宥之。

translations.literal: Mengxun attacked Jiao Lang and killed him — Qian Daxin's Investigations into the Twenty-two Histories says: "The Jin Shu says he attacked Lang, captured him, and spared him."
translations.idiomatic: On Mengxun attacking Jiao Lang and killing him: Qian Daxin's Investigations into the Twenty-two Histories notes that the Jin Shu says he took Lang and then spared him.

sentences.zh: 與此傳不同。」

translations.literal: " This differs from this biography."
translations.idiomatic: " That account disagrees with this biography."

sentences.zh: 追到西支澗 「澗」各本並作「間」，據魏書盧水胡沮渠蒙遜傳、晉書載記改正。

translations.literal: Pursued to Xizhi Stream — "jian (stream)" in all editions reads "jian (interval)," corrected according to the Wei Shu biography of the Lushui Hu Juqu Mengxun and the Jin Shu annals.
translations.idiomatic: On the pursuit to Xizhi Stream: every edition reads "interval" for "stream," emended per the Wei Shu Juqu Mengxun biography and Jin Shu annals.

sentences.zh: 「西支」魏書、晉書作「解支」，錢大昕廿二史考異云：「解當作鮮，鮮西聲相近也。」

translations.literal: "Xizhi" in the Wei Shu and Jin Shu reads "Xiezhi"; Qian Daxin's Investigations into the Twenty-two Histories says: "Xie should read Xian; Xian and Xi are near in sound."
translations.idiomatic: "Xizhi" appears as "Xiezhi" in the Wei and Jin histories; Qian Daxin argues Xie should be Xian — the sounds xian and xi are close.

sentences.zh: 恂武衞將軍宋承廣武將軍張弘舉城降 各本並脫「張」字，據晉書涼武昭王傳補。

translations.literal: Xun Martial Guard General Song Cheng and Broad Martial General Zhang Hong surrendered the city — all editions omit the character "Zhang," supplied according to the Jin Shu biography of the Martial and Illustrious King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On Xun Martial Guard General Song Cheng and Broad Martial General Zhang Hong surrendering the city: all editions drop Zhang, restored from the Jin Shu biography of the Liang Martial and Illustrious King.

sentences.zh: 執蒙遜從弟成都從子日蹄頗羅等而去 「日蹄」通鑑宋文帝元嘉二年作「白蹄」。

translations.literal: Seized Mengxun's younger cousin Chengdu, his nephew Riti, Peluo, and others and departed — "Riti" in the Zizhi Tongjian for the second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song reads "Baiti."
translations.idiomatic: On taking Mengxun's cousin Chengdu, his nephews Riti and Peluo, and leaving: the Comprehensive Mirror (Song Emperor Wen, Yuanjia year 2) reads Baiti for Riti.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜第三子茂虔時為酒泉太守 「茂虔」御覽一二四引十六國春秋北涼錄、晉書載記同宋書。

translations.literal: Mengxun's third son Maoqian was then Jiuquan Administrator — "Maoqian" in Imperial Readings 124, citing the Northern Liang Records, and the Jin Shu annals agrees with the Song Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On Mengxun's third son Maoqian as Jiuquan administrator: Imperial Readings 124 (Northern Liang Records) and the Jin Shu annals match the Song Shu reading.

sentences.zh: 魏書、通鑑作牧健。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu and Zizhi Tongjian read Mujian.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Shu and Comprehensive Mirror read Mujian.

sentences.zh: 錢大昕廿二史考異云：「茂虔，北史作牧犍。

translations.literal: Qian Daxin's Investigations into the Twenty-two Histories says: "Maoqian — the Beishi reads Mujian."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin's Investigations into the Twenty-two Histories notes: "Maoqian — the Northern History has Mujian."

sentences.zh: 茂牧聲相近，犍與虔同音。」

translations.literal: Mao and Mu are near in sound; jian and qian are homophones."
translations.idiomatic: Mao and mu sound alike; jian and qian are the same in pronunciation."

sentences.zh: 乘丘先生三卷 「乘丘」元龜二三二作「桑丘」。

translations.literal: Master of Chengqiu, three juan — "Chengqiu" in the Yuan Gui 232 reads "Sangqiu."
translations.idiomatic: On the Master of Chengqiu in three juan: the Yuan Gui (juan 232) reads Sangqiu.

sentences.zh: 隋書經籍志雜家：「梁有桑丘先生書二卷，晉征南軍師楊偉撰，亡。

translations.literal: Suishu Bibliographic Treatise, Miscellaneous Schools: "Liang had the book of Master Sangqiu in two juan, composed by Jin Staff Officer of the Army Who Conquers the South Yang Wei — lost."
translations.idiomatic: The Suishu bibliography (Miscellaneous Schools) records: "Liang held the Master of Sangqiu in two juan, by Jin's staff officer of the Army Who Conquers the South, Yang Wei — now lost."

sentences.zh: 」章宗源考證云：「案宋書大且渠蒙遜傳『乘丘先生』，即此『桑丘先生』也。

translations.literal: " Zhang Zongyuan's Textual Verification says: "The 'Master of Chengqiu' in the Song Shu biography of the Great Juqu Mengxun is this 'Master of Sangqiu.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Zongyuan's verification argues that the Song Shu's "Master of Chengqiu" in the Great Juqu Mengxun biography is this same "Master of Sangqiu."

sentences.zh: 生下當有書字。」

translations.literal: Below "born" the character "book" should be present."
translations.idiomatic: The character for "book" should follow "composed."

sentences.zh: 第六弟武興縣侯儀德為征東將軍秦州刺史都督丹嶺以西諸軍事張掖太守 「儀德」魏書、通鑑作「宜得」。

translations.literal: The sixth younger brother, Marquis of Wuxing County Yide, as Grand General Who Conquers the East, Qin Inspector, Commander of Military Affairs West of Dan Ridge, and Zhangye Administrator — in the Wei Shu and Zizhi Tongjian the name is written Yide (with the characters for 'suitable' and 'obtain').
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth brother, Marquis of Wuxing Yide, as grand general who conquers the east, Qin inspector, commander west of Dan Ridge, and Zhangye administrator: the Wei Shu and Comprehensive Mirror write the name as Yide (a different character pair, same pronunciation).

sentences.zh: 高昌城主闞爽告急 「闞」各本並作「闕」，據北史改。

translations.literal: Gaochang city lord Kan Shuang reported urgency — "Kan" in all editions reads "Que," changed according to the Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaochang's lord Kan Shuang reporting distress: every edition reads Que for Kan, emended per the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 北史西域傳：「太武時，有闞爽者，自為高昌太守。

translations.literal: Beishi Western Regions zhuan: "In Emperor Taizu's time there was Kan Shuang, who made himself Gaochang Administrator."
translations.idiomatic: The Northern History's Western Regions account says: "Under Emperor Taizu there was Kan Shuang, who installed himself as Gaochang administrator."

sentences.zh: 」其後闞伯周為高昌王。

translations.literal: " Afterward Kan Bozhou became King of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Kan Bozhou became king of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 無諱遣將衞尞夜襲高昌 「衞尞」魏書作「衞興奴」。

translations.literal: Wuhui sent the general Wei Liao to night-raid Gaochang — "Wei Liao" in the Wei Shu reads "Wei Xingnu."
translations.idiomatic: On Wuhui sending general Wei Liao to raid Gaochang by night: the Wei Shu reads Wei Xingnu.
